entry.title: The economic cost of quantum advantage in computational chemistry and when quantum computing beats classical methods
entry.summary: The Price of Quantum Advantage in Computational Chemistry arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper examines 26 chemistry benchmark systems, including FeMoco, iron-sulfur clusters, cytochrome P450 and ruthenium catalysts, using the SHCI and TrimCI configuration interaction solvers. It compares classical computing workloads with fault-tolerant quantum resource estimates to calculate a break-even hourly price for a whole quantum processor. The results indicate that classical computation remains cheaper for six of seven systems even at an optimistic price, with FeMoco sensitive to the classical method used. The authors also analyze how orbital choice affects the determinant support needed for target-state overlap in quantum phase estimation.

entry.title: Neural network decoders that account for qubit loss in quantum error correction
entry.summary: Neural Network Decoders For Qubit Loss arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper presents a loss-aware convolutional neural network (CNN) decoder framework and a new sampler, slim, for training and simulating circuits with Pauli and loss errors. On the surface code, the decoder matches the accuracy of computationally expensive most-likely error (MLE) decoders at much lower latency. For the [[144,12,12]] bivariate bicycle (Gross) code, at physical error rates below 1%, the authors observe a logical error rate more than 10^3 times lower under a pure loss model than under a pure Pauli model at the same physical error rate, with enhanced sub-threshold scaling. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a loss-aware CNN decoder and sampler slim, matching MLE accuracy on the surface code at lower latency and reporting over 10^3-fold lower logical error rates on the [[144,12,12]] Gr

entry.title: Exact limit on how many neighbors can steer a multimode Gaussian node
entry.summary: Exact monogamy of steering and remote Wigner negativity for multimode Gaussian nodes arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper studies how many neighbors can steer a quantum optical node with k modes when the Gaussian states are linked through a network. For Gaussian measurements, it shows the exact limit is 2k-1, regardless of squeezing, amplification or noise. The same number also bounds how many neighbors can be made Wigner negative by a heralded non-Gaussian operation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove that Gaussian multimode nodes can be steered by exactly 2k-1 neighbors and extend the same count to remote Wigner negativity.

entry.title: Bound magic states in multi-qubit systems
entry.summary: Bound magic in multi-qubit systems arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper proves that some multi-qubit nonstabilizer states cannot yield pure magic, even with arbitrarily many copies and rounds of stabilizer operations. The authors introduce a PPT-like criterion for magic that is closed under tensor products and stabilizer operations and reduces to the stabilizer polytope for one and two qubits. Using this criterion, they prove the existence of multi-qubit bound magic and explicitly construct such states for three or more qubits. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove multi-qubit bound magic exists, introduce a PPT-like criterion for magic, and give explicit constructions for n≥3 qubits.

entry.title: Which quantum-state transformations are allowed under a general class of free operations in texture resource theory
entry.summary: State convertibility in quantum-state texture from a general form of free operations arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper studies which transformations between quantum states are permitted in the quantum-state texture resource theory. It fully characterizes free operations in arbitrary finite dimension and derives an exact deterministic conversion criterion for mixed states in higher dimensions. The criterion reduces to a search problem that can be solved with semidefinite programming. The characterization can also be used to study probabilistic and assisted manipulation of quantum-state texture. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give an exact deterministic conversion criterion for mixed states in arbitrary finite dimension via a decomposition of free operations into filter and CP map, reducible to SDP.

entry.title: Monotonic measures of asymmetry and how robust the quantum Mpemba effect is
entry.summary: Monotonic probes of asymmetry and robustness of the quantum Mpemba effect arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies a family of asymmetry measures based on sandwiched Rényi divergences, which are monotonic under symmetry-preserving quantum channels. The authors develop a two-parameter replica approach to compute these quantities from charged moments and show a correspondence with conventional Rényi asymmetries under the inversion of the Rényi index. For quenches from tilted ferromagnetic states, they find that the quantum Mpemba effect occurs throughout the entire family of these monotones. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build sandwiched Rényi asymmetry monotones, establish an α↔1/α correspondence with conventional Rényi asymmetries, and test quantum Mpemba robustness in quenches.

entry.title: How the copies needed to certify typical pure quantum states change sharply
entry.summary: Sharp Transitions of Copy Complexity in Local Certification of Typical Pure States arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper determines how many copies of an n-qudit quantum state are needed to certify it using tensor-product measurements. The optimal number scales as Θ(n^r), where the exponent r is a piecewise constant function of g=(a-b)/(1-b), and the authors give an exact algorithm for its breakpoints. The result holds for families of pure target states whose Haar measure tends to one as n grows. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report exact copy-complexity exponents with piecewise-constant dependence on g, matching upper and lower bounds under tensor-product measurements.

entry.title: Magic Moments: Certifying Quantum Nonstabilizer Resources from Few Copies
entry.summary: Magic Moments: An Operational Approach of Certifying Nonstabilizerness from Few Copies arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper proposes a criterion that certifies magic, the nonstabilizerness resource needed for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation, using a few moments of the discrete Wigner function rather than full reconstruction. For pure states of any number of qudits, the criterion is necessary and sufficient, while for mixed states the authors build a hierarchy of higher-moment conditions reaching the exact negativity threshold. Each moment is measurable as a two-outcome observable's expectation on a few state copies, using a constant-depth Clifford circuit with a round count independent of qudit number. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a moment-based magic certification criterion, necessary and sufficient for pure states and reaching the exact negativity threshold for mixed states via higher-moment hierarchies.

entry.title: Planckian lower bound on thermalization time for strongly coupled open quantum systems
entry.summary: Planckian bounds on thermalization times of strongly coupled open quantum systems arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper examines whether the thermalization time of strongly coupled open quantum systems, whose equilibrium state is the mean-force Gibbs state, is bounded by the Planckian time scale ħ/k_B T. By requiring the same process to thermalize a family of nearby system Hamiltonians, it derives a lower bound independent of specific system-bath dynamics. The bound depends only on the distinguishability of the mean-force Gibbs states and can be computed from equilibrium properties. It is characterized in exactly solvable fermionic models, the spin-boson model, and a spin coupled to a two-dimensional Heisenberg antiferromagnet. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive a system-bath-independent Planckian lower bound on thermalization time from equilibrium quantities, characterized across several strong-coupling models.

entry.title: A proof of error bounds for a transverse spin-gradient approximation in noncollinear spin density theory
entry.summary: The transverse spin-gradient approximation in noncollinear spin density functional theory arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper proves a quantitative error bound for a fixed-axis variant of the transverse spin-gradient approximation in noncollinear spin density functional theory. It uses a spin-spiral wave as the local reference, writing the energy as an integral depending on the total density, the magnetization and its first derivatives. When the relevant length scale is N^{1/3}, the error is O(N^{5/6}) for an energy of order N. Setting the spiral phase to zero recovers the noncollinear local spin density approximation for arbitrary magnetization directions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a quantitative error bound for a fixed-axis transverse spin-gradient approximation using spin-spiral waves as local reference in noncollinear DFT.

entry.title: "Gaussian Is All You Need": Renyi Optimizers and Optical Channel Simulation
entry.summary: Gaussian Is All You Need: Renyi Optimizers and Optical Channel Simulation arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies how much entanglement is needed to prepare an entangled state and how fidelity falls when less is available. The authors prove that for any finite-energy multimode bosonic Gaussian state, the entanglement cost and Renyi entanglement of formation of orders above one are additive and attained by a Gaussian pure-state decomposition. Consequently, the closest separable state in fidelity to a Gaussian state is Gaussian, and the strong converse exponent of entanglement dilution can be computed exactly. For channels, pure Gaussian inputs minimize output Renyi entropies of multimode Gaussian channels, and the optimal fidelity of simulating pure-loss and quantum-limited amplifier channels with finite entanglement is obtained. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove additivity of Rényi entanglement measures for multimode Gaussian states and that pure Gaussian inputs minimize output Rényi entropies of Gaussian channels.

entry.title: Bound entanglement with negative partial transpose exists
entry.summary: Bound Entanglement with Negative Partial Transpose Exists arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper examines a Werner state on C^8 ⊗ C^8 with density matrix (23I − 3SWAP)/1448. It shows that this state has a negative partial transpose and is bound entangled, so no LOCC protocol can distill entanglement from any number of copies. Even with separable operations, the fidelity of a two-qubit output with a Bell state stays at or below about 0.604. The authors conclude that distillable entanglement is neither additive nor convex. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors exhibit a specific Werner state with negative partial transpose that is bound entangled, implying distillable entanglement is neither additive nor convex.

entry.title: Proof that AC⁰ is not contained in BQAC⁰/qpoly via sublinear-degree Pauli approximation
entry.summary: mathsfAC⁰ notsubseteq mathsfBQAC⁰/mathsfqpoly via Sublinear-Degree Pauli Approximation arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper proves that AC⁰ is not contained in BQAC⁰/qpoly in the single-copy, single-output model, using an explicit P-uniform family of linear-size monotone depth-2 CNFs. It approximates the acceptance operator of any QAC⁰ circuit by an advice-independent Hermitian operator of sublinear Pauli degree. The same approximation gives two stretched-exponential bounds for QAC⁰ circuits acting on m-qubit states. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a sublinear-Pauli-degree operator approximation for QAC⁰ circuits with quantum advice, separating AC⁰ from BQAC⁰/qpoly and deriving two stretched-exponential bounds.

entry.title: Paper showing the asymptotic spectrum of tensors is path-connected
entry.summary: The asymptotic spectrum of tensors is connected arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper proves that the asymptotic spectrum of complex tensors of every fixed order k≥3 is path-connected, so every spectral point links by a path to each one-leg-versus-rest flattening rank. As a result, the asymptotic spectrum at any fixed tensor is a closed interval, answering a question of Strassen. The authors also develop a general interpolation method between spectral points and use it to give new results and simpler proofs about rectangular matrix multiplication and polynomial multiplication. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove path-connectedness of the asymptotic tensor spectrum for every fixed order, answering Strassen, via a general interpolation method.

entry.title: Noise threshold for quantum-memory-assisted learning
entry.summary: Noise threshold for learning with quantum memory arXiv · Nov 25, 2026Quantum memories can exponentially reduce the number of experiments needed to learn a physical process, but real memories are noisy. The paper shows that for Pauli memory noise, this advantage depends on the sum of the squared eigenvalues. It proves that when this sum is at most one, no protocol with an entangled probe gains an exponential advantage. Experiments on a superconducting processor and a three-qubit repetition code are also reported. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive a noise threshold for quantum-memory learning advantage under Pauli noise, prove no exponential gain below it, and report superconducting-processor experiments.

entry.title: Exact exponents for trace-distance errors in quantum information tasks
entry.summary: Exponential Analysis for Trace-Distance Errors in Quantum Information Theory arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies trace-distance errors in classical-quantum soft covering, privacy amplification against quantum side information, convex splitting, and decoupling by Haar-random unitaries followed by partial trace. For independent and identically distributed settings, it determines exact reliability functions and strong converse exponents for these tasks. The reliability formulas involve sandwiched Rényi information, while the strong converse exponents involve Petz-Rényi information. The proofs link trace-distance errors to quantum hypothesis testing. ★★★★ Notable: The authors determine exact reliability functions and strong converse exponents for several quantum tasks, using sandwiched and Petz-Rényi information and hypothesis testing.

entry.title: Vacuum correlation measures expressed as CFT partition functions
entry.summary: Vacuum correlation measures as CFT partition functions arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper shows that in any d-dimensional CFT, the vacuum sandwiched Rényi mutual information of integer order n between two disjoint balls maps to a partition function on a manifold with topology #^{n-1}(S^1×S^{d-1}). At n=2 it equals the thermal partition function on S^{d-1}, which upper-bounds the von Neumann mutual information. For n>2 the quantity diverges at finite separation due to a hot-spot limit, and explicit CFT evaluations agree well with density matrix computations.

entry.title: Two complementary ways critical quantum systems can sharpen parameter estimation
entry.summary: Complementary mechanisms of critical quantum metrology arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper proposes a second mechanism for critical quantum metrology, based on suppressed quantum noise rather than enhanced response to a parameter. It studies coherently radiating spin states (CRSS) of N spin-1/2 particles, which show a second-order transition at r=1. Near criticality, estimating r benefits from enhanced susceptibility, while estimating the phase φ benefits from suppressed noise, and both reach an error scaling of about N^(-2/3), better than the standard quantum limit of N^(-1/2).

entry.title: The energy cost of objectivity: how much work it takes to make an event a shared fact
entry.summary: The thermodynamic budget of objectivity arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper examines when an event becomes an objective fact, meaning enough independent physical records exist that no operation can leave every observer ignorant of it. The authors compute the thermodynamic costs of creating, keeping, and destroying such records exactly, using a minimal model in which a driven central qubit writes records into N initially thermal registers. They report that the work needed to create a record grows linearly with redundancy at the Landauer coefficient, and that recording in a basis misaligned beyond a critical angle makes objectivity unreachable at any work.

entry.title: Schrödinger's Legacy: The Wave Function and Quantum Reality
entry.summary: Schrödinger's Legacy: The Wave Function and Quantum Reality arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper examines how Schrödinger developed wave mechanics and how his work shaped the philosophy of quantum mechanics, with a focus on the metaphysics of the wave function. He interpreted the wave function as electron charge density, an idea later replaced by Born's statistical interpretation but revived in modern realist approaches such as the mass-density and multi-field interpretations. The paper also notes its usefulness in quantum chemistry for computing the shapes of atoms and molecules. It argues that this realist tradition paved the way for ongoing attempts to define a clear ontology of the microscopic world.

entry.title: Sampling Rare Transition Paths in Non-Markovian Open Quantum Systems
entry.summary: Transition Path Sampling for Rare Events in Non-Markovian Open Quantum Systems arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper extends transition path sampling to non-Markovian quantum state diffusion, which is exact for Gaussian baths. The method therefore applies to non-Markovian and strongly coupled open quantum systems. For tunneling from the normal to the superradiant state in the unbalanced open Dicke model, the authors compute probabilities down to 10^-8 and rates that brute-force approaches cannot reach.

entry.title: Computing several excited states at once with double bracket flows
entry.summary: Simultaneous computation of multiple excited states via double bracket flows arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper proposes a framework that simulates multiple excited states simultaneously using dynamical flows, relevant to strongly correlated many-body systems and molecular electronic structure. A single common double bracket flow drives different pure initial states toward different target excited states without requiring prior information about them. The authors establish a necessary condition for convergence and a sufficient condition for exponential convergence. Two scheduling strategies are introduced: Chebyshev scheduling and adaptive scheduling.

entry.title: Quantum-state rugosity as a measurement-induced relative entropy
entry.summary: Rugosity as a measurement-induced relative entropy arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies quantum-state rugosity, which measures how far a quantum state departs from the flat superposition of a given basis. The authors show that rugosity equals the classical relative entropy produced by a binary flat-state measurement. This gives hypothesis-testing interpretations: it is the asymptotic discrimination exponent under repeated flat-state measurements and the exact finite-copy exponent under unrestricted quantum testing with zero type-I error.

entry.title: A integrable splitting method for simulating a nonlinear flow on quantum computers
entry.summary: The integrable Lie-Trotter-Suzuki decomposition for nonlinear dynamics: Efficient Hamiltonian simulation of the Stepanoff flow arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper proposes the integrable Lie-Trotter-Suzuki decomposition (I-LTS), a unitary time-integration method for nonlinear dynamical systems. The generator is split into integrable parts, and a Lie-Trotter-Suzuki decomposition of a chosen order approximates the full evolution operator. The method is applied to the Stepanoff flow on the torus, with a quantum algorithm built from alternating quantum Fourier transforms and quantum signal processing circuits. The circuit was run on a numerical emulator of fault-tolerant quantum computers, and the results agreed with several classical methods.

entry.title: Fewer parameters, longer runtimes: the real time cost of hybrid quantum physics-informed neural networks
entry.summary: Fewer Parameters, Longer Runtimes: The Wall-Clock Cost of Hybrid Quantum Physics-Informed Neural Networks arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper compares a classical physics-informed neural network (PINN) with four hybrid quantum-classical versions on a one-dimensional seawater temperature diffusion problem, with quantum circuits simulated on a CPU. It times each stage of training and finds the hybrids are much slower than the classical PINN, and still slower than size-matched classical controls. Runtime rises rapidly with the number of qubits. The authors conclude that having fewer trainable parameters does not mean lower computational cost.

entry.title: Rényi multi-entropy computed from Riemann surfaces
entry.summary: Rényi multi-entropy from Riemann surfaces arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper computes vacuum tripartite Rényi multi-entropy in a two-dimensional compact-boson conformal field theory. For each integer Rényi index, the partition function is evaluated on the replica Riemann surface for disjoint intervals, giving a twist four-point function written as a ratio of theta functions. The adjacent three-point coefficient is obtained independently from a Fermat curve. The predictions agree with lattice results for critical XXZ and Ising spin chains and a harmonic chain, and the paper also presents a unitary CFT where the canonical replica construction gives complex Rényi multi-entropy.

entry.title: Direct generation of N00N states using layered semiconductors
entry.summary: Direct generation of N00N states with layered semiconductors arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper demonstrates generating tunable two-photon polarization N00N states directly from a subwavelength-thick 3R-MoS2 flake. The pump polarization sets the N00N state basis without changing its structure or generation efficiency. The source removes the need for interferometric optics, enabling compact quantum-enhanced polarization interferometry.

entry.title: Experimental benchmarks of non-Clifford hypergraph states and nonlocal games on IBM superconducting quantum chips
entry.summary: Experimental Quantum Hardware Benchmarks of Flat Non-Clifford Hypergraph States, Antipodal Obstructions, and Nonlocal Games on IBM Heron r2 arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper reports experiments on two 156-qubit IBM Heron r2 processors using non-Clifford hypergraph states defined by discrete algebraic invariants. It verifies antipodal obstructions and mod-17 Walsh rigidity, and tests coherence with Loschmidt echoes on states up to 16 qubits. It also runs nonlocal games, including Mermin-Peres, GHZ parity, and Hardy/Guhne-Cabello games, reporting win rates above classical bounds on qubit counts from 3 to 30.

entry.title: Slow mixing of Gibbs sampling in the quantum Curie-Weiss model
entry.summary: Slow mixing of Gibbs sampling for the quantum Curie-Weiss model arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies how quickly a Gibbs sampler mixes in the quantum Curie-Weiss model, a model of a quantum magnet. The authors show that at fixed low temperature and weak transverse field, the Chen-Kastoryano-Gilyen Gibbs sampler has a mixing time that is exponentially large, so thermalization is very slow. They also propose a dynamical quantum bottleneck theory that generalizes the classical notion of conductance, and give a complementary explanation of the slow mixing using an effective Fokker-Planck equation.

entry.title: Self-learning quantum Monte Carlo enhanced by Rydberg-atom measurement data
entry.summary: Data-enhanced self-learning projective quantum Monte Carlo with Rydberg-atom measurements arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper introduces a data-enhanced self-learning projective quantum Monte Carlo (PQMC) method that feeds projective measurements from programmable quantum simulators into the guiding wavefunction used for ground-state projection. The approach is demonstrated on a two-dimensional Rydberg-atom array with restricted Boltzmann machine and recurrent neural network guiding wavefunctions. Experimental pretraining reduces finite-population effects and speeds up self-learning convergence, with a more pronounced benefit for the RBM.

entry.title: Why single photons form interference fringes: mode phase versus state phase
entry.summary: Why do single photons produce interference fringes? The phase of a mode and the phase of a state arXiv · Nov 26, 2026These lecture notes start from Maxwell's equations, expand the electromagnetic field in vector modes, and quantize it, introducing the quantity measured by a photodetector. They explain that the word "phase" refers to two different things: the phase of a mode, set by the optical setup, and the phase of the quantum state exciting that mode. The authors conclude that only the mode phase determines the interference fringes.

entry.title: Motion of a charged particle on a conformal helicoidal surface
entry.summary: Dynamics of a Charged Particle on a Conformal Helicoidal Surface arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies the classical and quantum motion of a charged particle on a conformal helicoidal surface embedded in four-dimensional Euclidean space. A uniform ambient magnetic field becomes a nonuniform field on the surface, and a cyclic longitudinal coordinate allows an exact transverse reduction. The authors classify single- and double-well regimes and derive exact transverse periods in the two double-well sectors, which diverge logarithmically at the separatrix. Intrinsic quantization yields an exact weighted transverse eigenvalue problem.

entry.title: Resource theory of π-ordered imaginarity and its quantifiers
entry.summary: Resource theory of pi-ordered imaginarity and its resource quantifiers arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper extends the standard resource theory of quantum imaginarity by imposing a permutation order π on diagonal populations, producing a π-ordered imaginarity framework. Free states must be real in a reference basis and have diagonal populations obeying the prescribed order, which separates complex phases from population misordering as two distinct resources. The authors characterize free states using majorization and the Schur-Horn theorem, and define resource quantifiers based on relative entropy, fidelity and robustness. They also derive inequalities linking π-ordered imaginarity robustness to π-ordered coherence robustness.

entry.title: Neutrino-oscillation thermometry: multi-temperature identifiability and noise benchmark
entry.summary: Conditional multiparameter thermometry with neutrino oscillations: MSW energy diversity and a plasma-noise benchmark arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper studies inference of two zone temperatures in a restricted two-flavor neutrino dephasing model with fixed electron densities. When both temperatures enter through a single accumulated dephasing exponent, the single-energy quantum Fisher information matrix has rank at most one, but energy-resolved samples with noncollinear thermal-sensitivity vectors restore local identifiability. An electron-only Debye-cell estimate of the longitudinal quantum signal-to-noise ratio is given, and complete phase averaging is shown to remove temperature information carried only by longitudinal coherence damping. The estimate is not a microscopic bound or a detector forecast.

entry.title: Quantum motion of a charged particle on rotating curved surfaces and curves in electromagnetic fields
entry.summary: Quantum dynamics of a charged particle on rotating curved surfaces and space curves in electromagnetic fields arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper builds a gauge-consistent framework for a charged particle confined to a rotating curved surface or curve in an electromagnetic field, starting from the covariant Klein-Gordon equation. Rotation appears as an effective gauge potential, while geometry enters separately as the da Costa potential. Three mechanisms are proposed to remove the coupling between gauge fields and geometry, and effects are examined on a torus and a corrugated quantum ring.

entry.title: Experimental test of how compilation order affects Grover-Rudolph probability loading on a three-qubit NMR processor
entry.summary: Experimental characterisation of compilation-dependent Grover--Rudolph probability distribution loading on a three-qubit NMR processor arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper loads probability distributions on a three-qubit liquid-state NMR processor using an ancilla-free Grover-Rudolph circuit compiled into Ry, X and CNOT gates. It compares logically equivalent versions that differ only in the order of CNOT controls and finds their measured accuracy differs, with the sign and size of the difference changing under gate removal and across repeated acquisitions. The authors favour the order and timing of executed pulses as an explanation but do not identify a mechanism.

entry.title: Native higher-order optimization using entropy quantum computing
entry.summary: Native higher-order optimization with entropy quantum computing arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper addresses optimization problems with cubic and quartic terms, which quadratic-only quantum annealers and most Ising machines cannot handle directly. The authors run six such instances from four industrial use cases natively on the Dirac-3S hybrid photonic-electronic system, without quadratization or circuit compilation. Dirac-3S returned feasible, distinct solutions but reached none of the reference optima, and classical methods matched or beat it at these sizes, so the reported gain is in expressibility and mapping cost rather than solution quality.

entry.title: Intrinsically nonlinear nanomechanical resonator aiming at the single-phonon Kerr regime
entry.summary: Intrinsically nonlinear nanomechanical resonator toward the single-phonon Kerr regime arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper uses strong intrinsic nonlinearity of a nanomechanical resonator instead of external nonlinear sources. The authors quantify it with a new method based on coupling between bending modes and estimate an upper bound of 34.0 ± 9.7 phonons for the onset of intrinsic mechanical bistability. They also propose a tuning mechanism based on the polarization angle of an upward-buckled nanotube resonator, and extrapolate that shorter resonators could reach the single-phonon Kerr regime.

entry.title: Coherent control of squeezed atomic states in Fourier-shaped optical lattices
entry.summary: Squeezing-preserving coherent control in Fourier-shaped optical lattices arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies how anharmonicity in an optical lattice's trapping potential degrades the motional squeezing of atoms. Numerical simulations show that adding a weak second or third spatial harmonic to a one-dimensional lattice slows the initial decay of squeezing. The authors attribute this to the optimal harmonic nearly equalizing the two dominant vibrational level spacings over the squeezed wave packet, which cancelling the quartic term alone does not achieve.

entry.title: Comparing detection methods for nanoscale NV-center NMR spectroscopy
entry.summary: On the performance of nanoscale detection methods in NV-center spectroscopy arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper addresses nuclear magnetic resonance detection in subfemtoliter volumes using nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond. It brings four protocols, Qdyne, CS, MCS, and CASR, into a single framework. The authors derive a unified analytical expression for signal-to-noise ratio and spin-number sensitivity applicable to all four, and numerical simulations of the full measurement sequences confirm it. The two metrics are then used to identify which protocol performs best in each experimental regime.

entry.title: Reusing trained parameters across quantum photonic chips with varied fabrication
entry.summary: Cross-chip transfer in quantum photonic neural networks arXiv · Nov 25, 2026Manufacturing variability makes it hard to reuse one set of trained parameters across a batch of quantum photonic chips without chip-specific tuning. The authors propose Monte Carlo ensemble training (MC-ENS), which optimizes one shared parameter set by averaging losses over simulated chip realizations drawn from a statistical model of fabrication errors. In simulations of CNOT synthesis and Ising dynamics, MC-ENS lowered mean conditional process infidelity and raised mean postselection probability on unseen chips.

entry.title: Search-for-Gradient: restart-by-search to escape flat regions in variational quantum algorithms
entry.summary: Search-for-Gradient: Search-Based Restarts for Optimisation in Structured Flat Landscapes of Variational Quantum Algorithms arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper proposes a search-based restart framework for variational quantum algorithms stuck in flat parameter landscapes where gradients vanish. When gradient-based updates stop, the method samples points to find regions with nonzero gradients and restarts local optimisation. The authors give theoretical estimates of jump counts and escape probability, and test the approach on synthetic functions and a real quantum circuit cost landscape.

entry.title: A quantum algorithm that directly estimates energy-level differences by simulating quantum dynamics
entry.summary: Quantum Algorithm for Direct Estimation of Energy-Level Differences via Quantum Dynamics Simulation arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper proposes a quantum algorithm for early fault-tolerant quantum computers that estimates tiny energy-level differences, such as energy gradients and molecular forces. It combines the time-evolution operators before and after a parameter shift into one circuit, followed by a non-adaptive statistical reconstruction in the energy-difference domain. Numerical simulations and resource estimates on systems such as the Fermi-Hubbard model show lower resource requirements at comparable precision.

entry.title: Speeding up transmon qubit readout with an ancillary transmon
entry.summary: Ancilla-Assisted Accelerated Readout of Transmon Qubits arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper proposes a method to speed up dispersive readout of superconducting transmon qubits. An extra ancillary transmon coupled to the same resonator is correlated with the target qubit using a fast CNOT gate, roughly doubling the resonator frequency shift. Using branch analysis to account for ionization and other nonlinearities, the authors report that measurement durations can be reduced to about 0.6 times the original, including realistic noise and gate times.

entry.title: Scaling laws for quantum reflection of hydrogen isotopes on silicon
entry.summary: Scaling laws for quantum reflection of hydrogen isotopes on silicon arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper calculates the quantum reflection probability of hydrogen isotopes H, D, and T striking the plane surface of intrinsic silicon. The results follow scaling laws determined by scattering lengths obtained from theory. The scattering lengths themselves also follow scaling laws with respect to the atomic masses of the isotopes.

entry.title: Correlations beyond quantum theory in a single-system pseudo-quantum model
entry.summary: Beyond-quantum correlations for single system in pseudo-quantum model arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper proposes a pseudo-quantum model for a single system, whose pseudo-states and effects satisfy all quantum properties except that they may have negative eigenvalues. Using the random access code communication game, the authors show that this model achieves a success probability above the optimal quantum value, producing beyond-quantum correlations. They further show these correlations violate the information causality principle, and that two non-orthogonal states can be perfectly distinguished within the model.

entry.title: Real-time cryogenic CMOS readout of photon number from a single SNSPD
entry.summary: Real-Time Cryo-CMOS Photon-Number Readout from a Single SNSPD arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper presents a cryogenic electronic circuit operating close to a superconducting nanostrip single-photon detector (SNSPD) inside the cryostat. The circuit isolates single-photon detection events directly from the SNSPD signal. This reduces photon-number readout latency to (13.9 ± 0.3) ns, enabling low-latency feedforward operations based on intrinsic photon-number measurements.

entry.title: A path integral method with far-field expansion for simulating open quantum systems interacting with a thermal bath
entry.summary: A Path Integral Method with Far-Field Expansion for Open Quantum Dynamics arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper links the quasi-adiabatic propagator path integral (QuAPI) method with fast resummation of Dyson series (FRODS). Building on this link, it introduces PIFFE, a path integral method with far-field expansion, for quantum systems linearly coupled to a thermal Gaussian bath. PIFFE combines QuAPI with a Taylor expansion of the far-field bath influence, keeping interactions within r time steps in exponential form. Spin-boson tests show results much closer to QuAPI than FRODS gives, while requiring substantially less storage than QuAPI.

entry.title: Preheating-like stabilization of entanglement entropy in the mixed-field Ising model
entry.summary: Prethermalization of entanglement entropy in the mixed-field Ising model arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies how weak breaking of integrability affects the growth of half-chain entanglement entropy for random product states in the mixed-field Ising model. Melting times at set entropy thresholds are used to characterize the departure from integrable dynamics and the appearance of intermediate entanglement plateaus. The analysis separates the melting of integrable dynamics from the later decay of a prethermal plateau.

entry.title: Smallest input size needed for one-shot zero-error quantum capacity superactivation
entry.summary: Minimal input dimension for superactivation of one-shot zero-error quantum capacity arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies the one-shot zero-error quantum capacity using noncommutative graphs of quantum channels. It proves that this capacity is additive for any finite set of channels with two-dimensional inputs. The authors also construct a pair of noncommutative graphs in three-dimensional matrix algebra that shows superactivation of the capacity. Together, the results show the minimum input dimension needed for this superactivation is 3.

entry.title: Testing a spin-dynamics approximation on the quantum phase transition in the Ising model
entry.summary: Discrete truncated Wigner approximation of the quantum phase transition in the transverse-field Ising model arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper tests the discrete truncated Wigner approximation (DTWA), a method for simulating large spin systems, on the transverse-field Ising model during a quantum phase transition. It covers one to three dimensions and all-to-all coupling, using slow and fast linear ramps. DTWA fails on the one-dimensional chain, behaving like classical thermalization, but in square and cubic lattices it places the onset of order near the quantum Monte Carlo critical point without reproducing the Kibble-Zurek scaling. For all-to-all coupling, it tracks the exact growth of the order parameter along the entire ramp.

entry.title: A unified quantum algorithm for preparing exact and asymptotic many-body scar states from Dicke states
entry.summary: Unified preparation of exact and asymptotic quantum many-body scars from Dicke states arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper proposes a unified quantum algorithm for preparing exact and asymptotic quantum many-body scar (QMBS) states in spin-1 XY, domain-wall-conserving, and Onsager scar models. Model-dependent isometries map exact scar states to Dicke states and asymptotic scar states to gapless magnon excitations of a spin-1/2 ferromagnetic Heisenberg chain. The method is intended to enable systematic studies of nonergodic dynamics on programmable quantum simulators.

entry.title: Quantum-circuit simulation of small-x dipole branching and its multiplicity fluctuations
entry.summary: Coherent quantum-circuit simulation of Mueller dipole branching at small x: multiplicity fluctuations and DIS phenomenology arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper builds a coherent quantum circuit for a finite-state version of Mueller dipole branching, a stochastic process at small x whose splitting rates depend on transverse geometry. Poisson-clock uniformization controls the number of updates, and event-history registers keep the splitting paths, with transition amplitudes prepared from local splitting rates. The circuit's multiplicity probabilities match the truncated-clock Markov result to numerical precision and agree with the continuous-time Markov-chain benchmark within about 7×10⁻⁴. The authors also simulate the continuous-coordinate Mueller cascade and compare its normalized fourth factorial moment with an equal-mean Yule process.

entry.title: Testing whether quantum-inspired machine learning really helps forecast returns in an emerging stock market
entry.summary: Empirical De-Quantization and Norm-Controlled Spectral Audit of Quantum Cognition Machine Learning in an Emerging Equity Market arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper audits quantum cognition machine learning (QCML) and variational quantum circuits on Moscow Exchange data from 2020 to 2025, combining daily equity prices with lagged macro news under realistic trading costs. The authors use capacity-matched operator swaps and random-matrix controls to isolate the effect of complex phases, noncommutativity, and entanglement. Out-of-sample, none of these quantum elements improved return ranking over classical controls, and normalized spectral-gap crisis detection fell below chance. The authors conclude the model behaves more like an adaptive classical smoothing kernel.

entry.title: Phonon-aware quantum memory transferring spin states in NV centers
entry.summary: Phonon-Aware Electron-to-Nuclear Spin Quantum Memory in NV Centers arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper models how the electron spin of a single nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond transfers its state to a nearby carbon-13 nuclear spin, a step in building quantum memory. The model includes hyperfine coupling, a microwave-assisted swap operation, coupling to a single phonon mode, and Lindblad relaxation and dephasing, and it is simulated with QuTiP. The results show that stronger spin-phonon coupling and higher temperature both reduce retrieval fidelity, which the authors use to identify operating regimes for NV-center quantum memory.

entry.title: Monotone crossing lattices for exact binary optimization encodings on Rydberg atom arrays
entry.summary: Monotone Crossing Lattices for Exact Binary Optimization Encodings on Rydberg Arrays arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper proposes a four-state unit-disk crossing cell that couples directly to adjacent cells, allowing nonlocal interactions on Rydberg atom arrays without auxiliary atoms. For the maximum-weight independent set problem, every ground state of the encoded instance decodes to an optimal solution, and binary quadratic objectives under pairwise Boolean constraints are encoded with an explicit constant offset. A rectangular variant also encodes minimum set cover, and across 18 paired benchmarks the layout reduces site counts by 12.1% to 54.0%.

entry.title: Unitary synthesis using a unary register to track data labels
entry.summary: Unitary Synthesis with a Unary Tracker arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies general unitary synthesis using a unary-encoded ancillary register that coherently tracks the computational-basis label of the data. This lets Boolean lookups use only CNOTs and shares precision-dependent synthesis cost across branches of each cosine-sine decomposition factor. For a classically specified n-qubit unitary with K mixing branches, the authors obtain T-count O(K+NL) with N+O(L) clean ancillas, where N=2^n and L=n+log(1/ε). Combined with the quantum Shannon decomposition, they also give space-depth volume O(N^2).

entry.title: LatentRL-QAS: Reinforcement learning in a latent space for transferring quantum circuit design across qubit counts
entry.summary: LatentRL-QAS: Transfer via Latent Reinforcement Learning for Quantum Architecture Search arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper introduces LatentRL-QAS, a framework that uses a circuit variational autoencoder to map quantum circuits with any number of qubits into a shared latent space, where a reinforcement learning agent searches for circuits. This design keeps the agent's state, actions, and network size fixed across qubit counts, enabling transfer of learned circuit representations. On absolutely maximally entangled (AME) states, the method discovered five- and six-qubit states and prepared them in 89-99% of evaluation episodes, and it remained robust under amplified depolarizing noise.

entry.title: High-speed GPU decoding for quantum error-correction codes under realistic circuit noise
entry.summary: High-Throughput GPU Decoding of Quantum Bivariate Bicycle Codes under Circuit-Level Noise arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents a parallel-window GPU decoder for bivariate bicycle (BB) quantum error-correcting codes, which are subject to circuit-level faults. The decoder combines reusable fault patterns, compact shared-memory state, and persistent GPU workers, using min-sum decoding with Relay-BP recovery. On an RTX 5090 it processes one syndrome round every 1 microsecond for all four evaluated codes, up to [[144,12,12]], and reports 120 times the throughput of sequential sliding-window decoding. For [[144,12,12]] at p=0.002, it reports a failure rate per round 36% lower than the published BP-SF result.

entry.title: Studying how geometry affects Differential Evolution and SOMA search on quantum state spaces
entry.summary: Geometry, masking and selection in Differential Evolution and SOMA on quantum state manifolds arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper examines how the geometry of non-vector search spaces, such as periodic angles, spheres and projective spaces, affects the core operations of Differential Evolution and SOMA. The authors keep the operators and selection rules fixed, change only the geometric primitives, and separate the effects of difference construction, masking and selection across many paired experiments. Geometry-consistent differences improve performance on most non-Euclidean configurations, and on six-qubit variational eigensolvers they reduce mean final loss by 90% for about 3% extra runtime.

entry.title: Testing methods to reduce coefficient-range limits on an 8-bit optimization machine
entry.summary: Coefficient-Range Mitigation on an 8-Bit Coherent Ising Machine arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper examines whether three techniques for handling limited coefficient ranges, originally studied for quantum annealing, improve end-to-end results on an 8-bit coherent Ising machine. Experiments on weighted Max-Cut, multidimensional knapsack, and quadratic assignment problems were conducted. The benefits were selective: moderate interaction extension raised mean best Max-Cut objectives while aggressive extension degraded performance, and bounded-coefficient encoding helped on only one knapsack instance. Augmented Lagrangian perturbations increased feasibility when unshifted penalties were too weak but did not outperform the best unshifted penalty setting.

entry.title: Quantum advantage in private hypothesis testing with entanglement and one classical bit
entry.summary: Quantum Advantage in Privacy-Preserving Hypothesis Testing via Entanglement-Assisted Classical Communication arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper asks whether quantum advantage in locally private hypothesis testing survives when users share entanglement with a server and send only classical messages. The authors introduce measurement local differential privacy and build protocols based on qubit measurement geometry, where each user sends one classical bit. They show the advantage persists for asymmetric and symmetric testing with input alphabets of size three or more in the high-privacy limit, with the error exponent ratio at least 5/4.

entry.title: Schism: Reconfigurable Scale-Up Domains for Distributed Quantum Computing
entry.summary: Schism: Reconfigurable Scale-Up Domains for Distributed Quantum Computing arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper proposes Schism, an architecture for switch-based quantum datacenters that lets programs dynamically change which quantum processing units share each Bell-state measurement resource pool. It aims to resolve the tradeoff between local communication contention and the optical loss of reaching idle resources elsewhere. Evaluated with SeQUeNCe using trapped-ion parameters on 32 QPUs, the authors report communication speedups of 4.9–7.3x over Fixed Clos connectivity and 3.6–8.3x over SwitchQNet across 11 workloads.

entry.title: How many events entanglement-based positronium imaging needs: information limits of CZT Compton polarimetry
entry.summary: Fisher-information limits of Compton polarimetry for entanglement-based positronium imaging with pixelated CZT detectors arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper examines how many detected photon events are needed when Compton polarimetry measures the polarisation correlation of annihilation photons, a proposed PET biomarker of tissue microstructure. The authors derive the classical Fisher information of double-Compton events about the correlation coefficient κ, compare it with the quantum Fisher information, and simulate pixelated CdZnTe detector rings. They find each event carries only a small fraction of the quantum limit, and event-wise maximum likelihood reaches the Cramér-Rao bound.

entry.title: Reducing T gates in product formulas using LLM agent loops
entry.summary: Reducing T gates in product formulas with agent loops arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper uses the Nemotron 3.5 Lightning language model in a coding-agent loop to optimize product formulas for quantum phase estimation, aiming to lower the T-gate cost on fault-tolerant quantum computers. The resulting protocol, ELOTE, reduced the median and geometric-mean T95 cost by 85.35% and 84.82% across 115 molecular Hamiltonians while meeting chemical accuracy on the training set. A further optimized δ-ELOTE protocol lowered geometric-mean T95 by 58.90% relative to ELOTE for ten reaction energies while preserving chemical accuracy. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use an LLM coding-agent loop to search product-formula structure and synthesis precision, yielding ELOTE; the report gives 85.35% median T95 reduction across 115 HamLib Hamiltonians, plus

entry.title: Sample Complexity of Quantum Function-State Tests for Monotonicity and Related Properties
entry.summary: Quantum Copy Complexity of Testing Monotonicity and Other Properties arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies how many copies of a quantum function state are needed to test whether a Boolean function is monotone. The authors give an improved tester with a better sample complexity upper bound than previously known, and prove the first nontrivial lower bounds for this task. The same framework also yields an Ω(n²) lower bound for testing union-closedness and 2-monotonicity. ★★★★ Notable: The authors improve the quantum function state monotonicity tester's sample complexity and give first nontrivial lower bounds, matching over a broad range of epsilon.

entry.title: When does a noisy Bell pair reach the Rains bound?
entry.summary: When does a noisy Bell pair attain the Rains bound? arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper studies two Bell-diagonal qubit states with the same singlet fraction and their achievable rates under operations that preserve the positive partial transpose. It shows that the Rains bound is reached only when one of the Bell probabilities is zero. Every mixed entangled isotropic state in any finite dimension lies strictly below its bound, implying the two-way quantum capacity of the qubit depolarizing channel is below its relative-entropy bound. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show PPT-preserving attainable rates of Bell-diagonal states can differ, giving an iff condition for attaining the Rains bound. They report strict gaps for all mixed isotropic states and i

entry.title: Exact optimal covariance-based entanglement tests for thermal states of the XY spin chain
entry.summary: Structure-factor witnesses of thermal entanglement: exact optimal covariance criteria for the XY chain arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies entanglement in thermal equilibrium states of the spin-1/2 XY chain in a transverse field. Using a covariance-matrix criterion that requires only one- and two-spin correlations, the authors show that the optimal witness for thermal states is determined by the momentum minima of three static spin structure factors, which scattering experiments can access. These witnesses certify entanglement and bound entanglement measures up to temperatures of the order of the exchange coupling, including in states with no pairwise entanglement. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show the optimal covariance-criterion witness for thermal XY-chain states is set by momentum minima of three static structure factors, with small-chain comparisons reported.

entry.title: Improved quantum algorithms for the traveling salesman problem and related problems
entry.summary: Improved Quantum Algorithms for TSP and More arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The traveling salesman problem (TSP) is a classic NP-hard optimization problem. This paper improves the best known quantum running time for TSP from O*(1.7274^n) to O*(1.70961^n). The method combines the Ambainis et al. framework with an extremal set-system approach, splitting the optimal tour into four consecutive subpaths and using amplitude amplification. The authors also give a new quantum space-time tradeoff for TSP and the same quantum upper bounds for several related problems. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine Grover search with extremal set systems, improving the quantum TSP exponent from 1.7274^n to 1.70961^n and giving a new space-time tradeoff.

entry.title: Optimal error bounds and exponents for universal randomness extraction against quantum side information
entry.summary: Sharp one-shot bounds and optimal exponents of universal randomness extraction arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies randomness extraction against quantum side information (privacy amplification) by relating it to hypothesis testing with quadratic constraints. It precisely determines the optimal scaling of the error of quantum privacy amplification in several regimes, using the standard trace-distance security criterion and focusing on universal hash function classes. The authors give one-shot converse bounds, establish the asymptotic i.i.d. error exponent of universal randomness extraction, and derive the exact strong converse exponent for 2-universal hash functions. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors relate privacy amplification to quadratically constrained hypothesis testing, giving optimal error scalings and tight strong converse exponents up to constant factors.

entry.title: Decoherent Histories via Local Spectral Dephasing in Quantum Many-Body Systems
entry.summary: Decoherent Histories from Local Spectral Dephasing in Quantum Many-Body Systems arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies local spectral dephasing as a mechanism producing decoherent histories in isolated quantum many-body systems. It proves that vanishing projector-weighted spectral concentration is asymptotically equivalent to vanishing time-averaged local memory. Under independently sampled waiting times and suitable conditions on the initial state and history weights, this local property suppresses normalized interference across complete fixed-length history families with high probability. For translation-invariant lattices, spectral estimates give conditions for dephasing at long times, illustrated by exact diagonalization and sparse time evolution of a spin chain.

entry.title: TyxonQ: A Quantum Computing Workflow Layer for Chemistry
entry.summary: TyxonQ: A Workflow Layer for Quantum Computing in Chemistry arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents TyxonQ, a workflow layer that connects quantum computing with classical treatments in computational chemistry, rather than focusing only on the hybrid quantum algorithm. Four integration interfaces link PySCF-compatible energy and force calculations and embedding, solver adapters, simulator and hardware backends, and classical simulation tools. The authors evaluate correctness, switching cost, reproducibility, and artifact portability on small chemistry workflows, distinguishing executed paths from source-level support.

entry.title: How many autonomous encoded qubits force isotropic noise response?
entry.summary: How Many Autonomous Encoded Qubits Force an Isotropic Noise Response? arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper studies how depolarizing noise and the autonomy of encoded qubits constrain each other. For dimension D=2^n≥4, autonomy forces isotropic noise response at about (D²+5)/3 generic encodings. For Pauli noise, a single generic encoding suffices.

entry.title: Reproducible energy-relaxation time distributions in superconducting qubits via broadband SWAP spectroscopy
entry.summary: Reproducible distributions of energy-relaxation times in superconducting qubits from broadband SWAP spectroscopy arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies the distribution of energy-relaxation times (T1) in superconducting qubits. The authors sweep the frequency of a flux-tunable qubit over several GHz and use the quality factor Q = 2πf01·T1 to compare results across frequencies. The cumulative distribution of Q pooled over the sweep is reproducible across four thermal cycles spanning 326 days. The broadband approach also distinguishes small coherence differences between identically designed qubits on two dies of the same wafer.

entry.title: An Efficient Quantum Algorithm for Solving the Generalized Geography Game
entry.summary: Efficient Quantum Algorithm for the Generalised Geography Game arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies the Generalized Geography Game, a two-player game on a directed graph in which players alternately move a token along edges without revisiting vertices. The authors present a bounded-error quantum polynomial-time (BQP) algorithm for solving this game. The algorithm runs in O(N²/ε⁶) time, polynomial in the input size N, with error ε = O(1/poly(N)).

entry.title: A bright, high-dimensional entangled photon-pair source using beam-like Type-II down-conversion
entry.summary: A bright source of high-dimensional spatially entangled photon pairs based on beam-like Type-II SPDC arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper demonstrates a bright source of high-dimensional spatially entangled photon pairs, generated through beam-like Type-II spontaneous parametric down-conversion in a β-barium borate crystal. Compared with a conventional collinear Type-I source, it shows about 1.56-fold higher single-photon count rate and about 1.45-fold higher coincidence count rate. Position correlation and momentum anti-correlation measurements certify at least 62-dimensional spatial entanglement within a 121-dimensional basis. The authors also use these correlations to demonstrate quantum imaging in both position and momentum domains.

entry.title: Structure theorem for quantum limit cycle attractors via a geometric path-integral approach
entry.summary: Structure theorem for quantum limit cycle attractors: A geometric path-integral approach arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper proves a structure theorem for a separable quantum system coupled through a symmetric bidirectional phase interface to a self-sustaining phase-oscillator environment. Under U(1) covariance, instantaneous Lindblad bounded positivity, and an entrainable periodic attractor, the reduced generator takes a universal form combining state-dependent coherent recoil with single-quantum feedback. The work also gives a dimensional dichotomy for dissipative saturation and an inverse coupling theorem requiring a non-trivial fundamental group for autonomous periodic orbits, with explicit implementations for a qubit, two qubits, and a bosonic Fock space.

entry.title: Late-time OTOCs in Toda Conformal Field Theory
entry.summary: Late-time OTOCs in Toda conformal field theory arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies late-time out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) of semi-degenerate primary fields in two-dimensional A_{N-1} Toda conformal field theory. In Liouville theory (N=2), the OTOC decays as t^{-3/2} when the continuum edge dominates, correcting a previously reported constant limit. For N=3, the spectral integral reduces to one dimension, and in the continuous phase the OTOC approaches a pure braiding phase. For N≥4, the same one-dimensional reduction violates a crossing bound in a positive diagonal expansion.

entry.title: Malus' Law vs. Wigner-Bell Inequality: Violation by Classical Light
entry.summary: When Malus' Law Meets the Wigner-Bell Inequality: Violation by Nonseparable Classical Light arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper studies a classical optical field with two nonseparable degrees of freedom and derives a Wigner-type probability bound from it. Joint probabilities given by normalized joint intensities, which follow Malus' law, violate this bound over a finite range of analyzer settings. The authors state that this violation does not imply spatial nonlocality or a failure of classical electrodynamics. Instead, it shows that context-dependent optical projection statistics are incompatible with a single global probability assignment.

entry.title: Superconductivity from Berry Connection of Many-Electron Wave Functions: U(1) Gauge Fluctuations and Invariance
entry.summary: Superconductivity from the Berry connection from many-electron wave functions: U(1) gauge fluctuation, gauge invariance, and superconductivity arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies electromagnetic U(1) gauge invariance and superconductivity using the Berry connection of many-electron wave functions and its fluctuations, which cause random transitions between quantum states. The authors treat gauge invariance in classical electrodynamics as a requirement that extracts the parts unaffected by gauge fluctuations. In quantum mechanics, they identify dissipation-free states arising from gauge fluctuations as superconducting states. The paper also explains a reversible superconducting-normal phase transition in a magnetic field, including force balance. The authors claim the theory resolves two fundamental disagreements between standard theory and experiment while retaining the main results of BCS theory.

entry.title: On-demand shaping of high-dimensional orbital angular momentum light states using a phase-only hologram
entry.summary: On-Demand Tailoring of High-Dimensional Orbital Angular Momentum States via a Phase-Only Hologram arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper proposes and experimentally demonstrates a method to shape both the amplitude and phase of high-dimensional orbital angular momentum (OAM) light states using only phase modulation. The measured fidelity stays above 80% even for a 128-dimensional state. The authors report higher generation efficiency than previous techniques, with the advantage growing as dimensionality increases.

entry.title: Dimensional crossover to a slow disordered spin bath below mean spin spacing
entry.summary: Dimensional crossover to a slow disordered spin bath below the mean spin spacing arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper examines how thin a layer of nitrogen spins around an NV⁻ centre in diamond must be to act as a two-dimensional spin bath. Using a cluster expansion that includes flip-flopping outer spins, it finds the crossover occurs near the mean spin spacing. Thin layers follow two-dimensional scaling with a prefactor six to seven times that of bulk, and without hyperfine disorder the crossover step is under three.

entry.title: Amatlas: A Coordination-Free 2D Array for Union-Find Quantum Error Decoding
entry.summary: Amatlas: A 2D Array Architecture for Union-Find Decoding Without Global Coordination arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents Amatlas, a two-dimensional array of processing elements for Union-Find decoding of the surface code, a method for real-time error correction in quantum computers. Each processing element handles one stabilizer on the qubit lattice and stores all measurement rounds locally, so every connection is between adjacent elements, and there is no central controller. Under circuit-level noise, its hardware implementation fits on an FPGA up to code distance 25, with an average of 462 ns per round at a 0.1% physical error rate. Amatlas reaches a threshold of 0.72%, compared with 0.78% reported for Union-Find decoding under the same noise model.

entry.title: Frequency Conversion of High-Dimensional Single-Photon Orbital Angular Momentum Comb States
entry.summary: High-Dimensional Single-Photon Frequency Conversion for Orbital Angular Momentum Comb State arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper proposes and experimentally demonstrates a scalable scheme for generating and frequency-converting high-dimensional single-photon orbital angular momentum (OAM) comb states. The authors prepared a single-photon OAM comb state with dimension up to 128, reaching a fidelity of 0.787 between reconstructed and target states and an effective dimension of 100. Using sum-frequency generation, they upconverted the state from the communication band to 520 nm visible light, and density matrix reconstruction confirmed that the OAM mode distribution and phase information were preserved.

entry.title: A scalable dense silicon qubit architecture with logical operations
entry.summary: A scalable dense silicon qubit architecture with logical operations arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper proposes a dense silicon spin qubit architecture for large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computing, made up of qubit memories, data qubit lanes, and cross junctions. Memories store logical qubits encoded with the rotated surface code, lanes use spin shuttling to connect logical qubits, and cross junctions handle routing and implement transversal logical CNOT gates. Using experimentally demonstrated parameters, the authors estimate that a code distance of at least 21 is needed for logical error rates below 10^-10 per syndrome cycle, and that over 120,000 logical qubits could fit on a 100 mm × 100 mm chip.

entry.title: Robust certification of non-projective qubit measurements without input randomness
entry.summary: Robust Certification of Non-projective Qubit Measurements without Inputs arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies how to robustly certify non-projective (POVM) qubit measurements using only the joint outcome distribution of two measurement devices, without relying on input randomness. The authors introduce a non-linear covariance witness that combines the geometry of projective measurements with a contraction bound valid for every two-qubit state. For noisy qubit singlets, they obtain exact critical white-noise fractions for trine and SIC-POVM measurements, and present explicit projective simulations reaching these thresholds.

entry.title: Infrared-absorption magnetometry in diamond nanocavities: demonstration and nanoscale limits
entry.summary: Infrared-absorption magnetometry in a diamond nanocavity: demonstration and limits at the nanoscale arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies a magnetometer based on infrared absorption by nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centres in diamond. Using spin-dense diamond nanocavities and probing cavity modes near the 1042 nm NV singlet transition, the authors demonstrate singlet-absorption magnetometry and cavity-enhanced magnetic field sensing for the first time. They also develop and experimentally validate a model that predicts the spin-dependent cavity response, the optimal operating conditions, and the practical limits of different optically detected magnetic resonance methods.

entry.title: A quantum instrument that steers rare quantum trajectories without post-selection.
entry.summary: Optimal Controlled Quantum Instrument for Monitored Many-Body Dynamics arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper addresses how to obtain rare outcomes of monitored quantum dynamics without post-selection, which would otherwise need exponentially many repeated experiments. The authors extend Bayes' rule to monitored many-body dynamics and bias quantum trajectories by nonlinear functions of the post-measurement state. They construct a quantum instrument on the system and an extra register, with a tensor-network representation. Examples include a precessing qubit and free fermions with gain and loss.

entry.title: NISQ Preparation of Conditional Thermal States for Precision Thermometry
entry.summary: NISQ Preparation of Conditional Thermal States for Precision Thermometry arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper prepares conditional thermal states, which are conditioned on a measurement apparatus's accessible pointer basis, for few-qubit systems on gate-based quantum computers. The experiments run on IonQ's cloud-based quantum computers across a range of temperatures. The authors validate the thermometry advantage by measuring the sub-quantum Fisher information of the prepared states, a lower bound on the quantum Fisher information that can be computed with a constant-depth circuit without tomography.

entry.title: Estimating Trotter error through phase analysis
entry.summary: Estimating the Trotter error via phase analysis arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper analyzes Trotter error using the spectrum of a phase operator constructed from the Hamiltonian. For small step sizes, it gives an estimate written as a sum of nested commutators of Hamiltonian terms. The estimate explains why general bounds are loose and remains more accurate than them at finite step sizes.

entry.title: Extracting usable entanglement from a noise-protected many-body system
entry.summary: Extracting Operational Entanglement from a Noise-Protected Many-Body System arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper studies a twelve-spin kicked Ising ring under collective dephasing, which evolves from a uniform product state into an entangled stationary state. Gates and measurements on each half of the ring herald a spin pair that teleports an unknown qubit with a mean fidelity of 90.5%. Simulations indicate that stronger noise correlations extend the time during which the ring produces pairs exceeding the classical teleportation limit.

entry.title: Embedding Quantum Error-Correcting Codes onto Hardware Lattices
entry.summary: Constructively Embedding Quantum Error-Correcting Codes arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents a constructive three-stage pipeline that maps a quantum error-correcting code's Tanner graph onto a hardware lattice: continuous embedding, grid assignment, and path routing. It compares three continuous embedding methods (multidimensional scaling, spectral embedding, and spring layout) using proxy metrics for footprint, communication overhead, and congestion. Ablation studies on the R2 HaPPY code find that graph-aware embedding and the routing algorithm matter more than grid assignment.

entry.title: Fluctuation relations for energy transfer at local causal horizons
entry.summary: Modular fluctuation relations on local causal horizons arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper studies horizon thermodynamics near a regular spacetime point using local causal horizons, going beyond mean energy and entropy balances. Using the modular structure of the horizon algebra and a thermal reference state, the authors construct a probability measure for boost-energy transfer and derive integral and detailed fluctuation relations, with mean entropy production given by the Araki relative entropy. For coherent scalar-field perturbations, they obtain a closed form for the characteristic function and a thermodynamic uncertainty relation bounding the variance by the mean transfer.

entry.title: Nitrogen-vacancy NMR detection of 15N spins in potassium nitrite-related nitrate solution
entry.summary: Nitrogen-Vacancy Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy of ¹⁵N Spins in Potassium Nitrite Solution arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper uses a microfluidic quantum sensor based on shallow nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond to detect 15N nuclear magnetic resonance from KNO3 solution at room temperature and low magnetic field. In femtoliter-scale sensing volumes, the measured magnetic-field variance reaches about 442 nT², roughly 43 times the expected statistical polarization. The 15N spin correlation decays within about 500 microseconds, limited mainly by the NV spin-lattice relaxation time rather than molecular diffusion, consistent with a KNO3 adsorption layer on the diamond surface.

entry.title: Calculating Floquet code distance via a static spacetime subsystem code
entry.summary: Using a static spacetime subsystem code to calculate Floquet code distance arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper maps the measurement sequence of a Floquet code to a static spacetime subsystem code. The authors show that this mapping preserves code distance, so the distance of a Floquet code can be computed from the corresponding static subsystem code. This turns the dynamical distance problem into a static one, simplifying analysis of Floquet measurement schedules and evaluation of fault tolerance for new schemes.

entry.title: Chiral Modes on Domain Walls in Topological Adaptive Quantum Dynamics
entry.summary: Chiral Domain-Wall Modes in Topological Adaptive Quantum Dynamics arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies 1+1D domain walls in 2+1D charge-conserving free-fermion dynamics driven by measurements and feedforward corrections. Each side of a wall is steered toward either a Chern insulator or a trivial insulator. The walls host topologically protected chiral modes whose entanglement and charge variance grow logarithmically, with algebraically decaying density correlations resembling a chiral free-fermion conformal field theory ground state.

entry.title: Can gauge symmetry still allow very shallow random quantum circuits?
entry.summary: Gauge symmetry permits extremely low-depth random unitary circuits arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies whether gauge symmetries limit symmetric unitary designs and pseudorandom unitaries, as continuous global symmetries do, using U(1) lattice gauge theories. It defines a randomization scale c, the minimum patch size needed for matter to screen all allowed boundary-flux mismatches, and a diffusive scale for boundary-flux correlations. The authors find that incomplete screening limits design guarantees to constant order, while complete local screening allows logarithmic-depth designs and pseudorandom unitaries.

entry.title: Non-Gaussianity as a resource for probing quantum criticality in bosonic systems
entry.summary: Bosonic Magic Resources at Quantum Criticality arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper quantifies non-Gaussianity in the ground state of the one-dimensional extended Bose-Hubbard model using quantum relative entropy, which depends only on one-body correlations. Scaling of this quantity with system size reveals quantum phase transitions involving hidden and conventional order. At the Mott-Haldane transition, subtracting the extensive background exposes a pronounced peak in the subleading contribution, signaling the onset of hidden string order.

entry.title: Quditology: using many energy levels for quantum information processing
entry.summary: Quditology: harnessing many levels for quantum information processing arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper reviews recent progress in using qudits, quantum systems with more than two levels, instead of standard two-level qubits for quantum information processing. It surveys experimental advances in high-fidelity preparation, control, and measurement of qudits on platforms including trapped ions, superconducting circuits, solid-state nuclear spins, photonic systems, and neutral atoms. The authors highlight early demonstrations of qudit-based simulation, computation, and error suppression, and outline key challenges and future directions for scalable qudit processing.

entry.title: Energy plateau cascades from complex-time local quenches in thermal 2D CFTs
entry.summary: Energy plateau cascades from complex-time local quenches in thermal two-dimensional CFTs arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies local operator quenches with complex-time evolution in thermal two-dimensional conformal field theories, which can serve as an effective description of conditional dynamics in a system coupled to an environment. Unlike vacuum quenches, the thermal initial state lets several conformal families take part in the evolution. The authors show that their competition can produce cascades of nearly homogeneous energy plateaux, with successive plateaux approaching the energies of different primary states. Conformal Ward identities on the cylinder and torus are used to compute the local energy density, illustrated in free-field theories, the Ising model and WZW models.

entry.title: Tensor-network study of the parton structure of mesons
entry.summary: Parton structure of mesonic states with tensor networks arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents the first direct tensor network calculation of flavor-resolved parton distribution functions for a pion-like isospin triplet in the (1+1)-dimensional two-flavor Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model. The mesons are prepared as bound states using staggered fermions and a charge-symmetrized Hamiltonian, and light-cone correlators are computed by real-time evolution. The quark and antiquark distributions obey the expected isospin relations, and the neutral pion shows equal u and d distributions. These results serve as benchmarks for quantum simulations of meson partonic structure.

entry.title: Theory of anomalous and superdiffusion in integrable spin chains
entry.summary: Theory of Anomalous Diffusion and Superdiffusion in Integrable Spin Chains arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies two-point correlations and current statistics in integrable spin chains, showing they can follow different universality classes. The authors use a multispecies particle gas that preserves the scattering structure of integrable spin chains to explain this separation. For anisotropy Δ>1, two-point correlations spread as Gaussian diffusion; at Δ=1, fluctuating hydrodynamics provides evidence for the KPZ (Kardar–Parisi–Zhang) scaling function in dynamical correlations.

entry.title: A new quantum lattice Boltzmann method for cosmological radiation transport
entry.summary: A novel quantum lattice Boltzmann methodology for cosmological radiation transport arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper proposes a new method for simulating radiation transport in cosmological codes using quantum lattice Boltzmann methods. Existing formulations give poor angular resolution for radiation point sources, and the authors introduce an angular redistribution approach that substantially improves resolution with minimal added complexity. The method is verified on both classical processors and quantum simulators, and the paper outlines how the quantum algorithm can be integrated into existing codes.

entry.title: QPAT: A General Quantum Machine Learning Framework for Quantum-Assisted Training and Classical Inference
entry.summary: QPAT: A Universal Quantum Machine Learning Framework for Quantum-Assisted Training and Classical Inference arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper proposes QPAT, a framework that uses a Quantum Circuit Born Machine (QCBM) as a learnable generative prior to guide the training of classical models. It can be integrated into backbones such as LSTMs, CNNs, and Transformers. Across six benchmarks in time-series forecasting, computer vision, and natural language processing, QPAT outperformed purely classical models in predictive performance and stability across random seeds.
