Inference is fully classical, avoiding quantum latency.

entry.title: Realistic runtime estimate for quantum-enhanced training of large machine learning models
entry.summary: A Realistic End-to-End Runtime Crossover Estimation for Quantum-Enhanced Training of Large-Scale Machine Learning Models arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper estimates the realistic end-to-end resource costs of training a linearized neural network with a quantum linear solver, including data access, computation, and readout. It analyzes three benchmarking scenarios of increasing complexity under different sparsity-scaling assumptions. The authors find that crossover points against classical methods appear only for very large problem sizes, long computation times, and highly restrictive output requirements.

entry.title: Gate-tunable spin splitting in Ge quantum well heterostructures for Andreev spin qubits
entry.summary: Gate-tunable spin splitting for Andreev spin qubits in Ge quantum well heterostructures arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper studies spin splitting in germanium-based superconductor-semiconductor heterostructures for Andreev spin qubits. Because Ge is a hole-based material, its spin-orbit coupling is cubic in momentum, unlike the linear coupling in InAs nanowires. The authors find that spin splitting in a planar Ge Josephson junction does not depend on junction width. They explore using this property to suppress charge trap effects, but note that charge traps also shift the chemical potential, which limits this approach.

entry.title: Generalized BEADS Representation: Visualizing Mixed Quantum States Completely
entry.summary: The Generalized BEADS Representation: A Correlation-Based Visualization of Mixed Quantum States arXiv · Oct 14, 2026This paper extends the BEADS representation, previously used for pure quantum states, to mixed quantum states. It introduces spherical functions, called beads, to visualize correlation structures, and uses a recursive optimization to find minimum-entanglement pure-state decompositions of subsystems. The correlation components are separated into total, genuine multipartite entanglement, quantum-discord-type, and classical correlations. The authors illustrate the representation on several classes of mixed states and show examples of entanglement distillation and noise channels.

entry.title: Low-degree torus approximations of the AND function and ACC⁰ circuits
entry.summary: Low-Degree Torus Approximations of the AND Function and mathsfACC⁰ Circuits arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper studies approximating Boolean functions by torus polynomials, real polynomials evaluated modulo one. It shows that the AND function has an ε-approximating torus polynomial of degree O(log(n/ε)), improving prior bounds. It also gives improved degree bounds for Boolean functions computed by depth-d, size-s AC⁰[m] circuits. The authors further prove that periodic Fourier representations and low-degree torus approximations are equivalent. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors improve the torus-polynomial approximation degree for AND from O(log²(n/ε)) to O(log(n/ε)), give an improved bound for AC^0[m] circuits, and show that periodic Fourier representations and

entry.title: Anomalous front spreading in quantum many-body transport with memory-dependent resetting
entry.summary: Anomalous front propagation in many-body quantum transport with memory-dependent resetting arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces an exactly solvable framework for non-Markovian quantum many-body dynamics based on stochastic resetting with memory, applicable to arbitrary time-independent Hamiltonians including interacting systems. The authors study domain-wall melting in a one-dimensional chain of noninteracting fermions, deriving exact analytical results for the density profile, front edge structure, extreme-value statistics of the rightmost fermion, and integrated current. They find that memory turns ballistic transport into logarithmically slow propagation, with the front edge broadening as √(ln t) and extreme-value statistics changing from Tracy–Widom to Gaussian. The mean and variance of the integrated current both grow logarithmically in time, and numerical simulations agree well with the predictions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce an exactly solvable memory-dependent resetting framework, derive analytic results for free-fermion domain-wall melting, and compare them with numerical simulations.

entry.title: Classical method for simulating fermion observables under particle-number-conserving quantum operations
entry.summary: Dirac Propagation for Simulating Fermionic Observables under Particle-Number-Conserving Unitaries arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces Dirac propagation, a classical method for simulating local observables in fermionic systems under particle-number-conserving unitary operations. The authors show that operator strings whose weight exceeds the total particle number can be discarded without error in the final expectation value. This exact cutoff keeps the number of retained strings polynomial in the number of modes at fixed particle number, including for interacting dynamics. The framework also supports simulating fermionic many-body dynamics and classically benchmarking fermionic quantum circuits. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce an exact operator-string cutoff at total particle number, bounding retained strings polynomially in modes, with explicit interacting-gate expressions for classical fermionic simu

entry.title: GHZ states of unbounded dimension from fixed-order multiphoton sources
entry.summary: Unbounded GHZ dimension from fixed-order multiphoton sources arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies the local dimension of GHZ states created by selecting events with exactly one photon in each output path. For two-photon sources the maximum local dimension is 2 for every even number of paths greater than 4. The authors show that three-photon sources can instead produce GHZ states of arbitrarily large local dimension. The proof models each source's three paths as an edge of a 3-uniform hypergraph, so accepted emission patterns correspond to perfect matchings, and the construction extends to r-uniform hypergraphs for any fixed r≥3. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show three-photon sources yield arbitrarily large local-dimension GHZ states via hypergraphs with many edge-disjoint perfect matchings, generalized to r-uniform hypergraphs.

entry.title: Optimal Trace Distance Estimation: a method for measuring how different two quantum states are, using the fewest samples possible.
entry.summary: Optimal Trace Distance Estimation arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper presents a trace distance estimator with optimal sample complexity for two unknown d-dimensional quantum states. It combines quantum tomography with polynomial approximation, using variance bounds derived from quantum Fourier analysis. The sample complexity matches the lower bound given by Wang (2026). ★★★★ Notable: The authors report an estimator matching the known lower bound of Wang (2026), combining tomography, polynomial approximation, and quantum Fourier analysis variance bounds.

entry.title: Second-order limits on quantum and private communication over erasure channels
entry.summary: Second-order asymptotics for the quantum and private capacities of the erasure channel arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper studies how much quantum or secret classical information an erasure channel can carry in finite blocks, where the channel either delivers a quantum system or signals that it was lost. It determines the optimal second-order coding rates for fixed infidelity, with a square-root correction term. The result covers entanglement transmission, entanglement generation, and private classical communication, with matching upper and lower bounds. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give matching second-order upper bounds for erasure-channel quantum and private capacities at every fixed infidelity, and show the privacy criterion affects the second-order term.

entry.title: Universal state merging for nearly i.i.d. quantum states
entry.summary: Universal state merging for almost i.i.d. states arXiv · Nov 24, 2026Quantum state merging transfers one party's share of a bipartite quantum state to another party while preserving its joint state with a purifying reference. For exactly i.i.d. copies, the optimal asymptotic net entanglement cost is S(A|B) ebits per pair. The paper shows this cost remains achievable under deviations from exact i.i.d. structure. A single sequence of one-way LOCC protocols, depending only on the state and a rate R above S(A|B), merges weakly almost i.i.d. sources with vanishing error. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show one LOCC merging protocol family achieves optimal S(A|B) cost universally over weakly almost i.i.d. sources, including Wasserstein and MSR subclasses.

entry.title: Classical algorithms for sparse random Hamiltonians using free probability
entry.summary: Classical algorithms for sparse random Hamiltonians via free probability arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper designs a classical algorithm for sparse random non-local Hamiltonians that accurately computes spectral fluctuations, thermal values, and time-ordered and out-of-time-order correlation functions. For any subexponential precision ε, the algorithm runs in time (1/ε)^{2+o(1)}, nearly identical to a quantum simulation. It first computes the model's mean behavior, then applies a short hierarchy of instance-dependent corrections that use free probability theory to predict long-time behavior from short-time data. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use free probability to design a classical algorithm for sparse random Hamiltonians, reporting near-quantum runtime for spectra, thermal values and correlators at late times.

entry.title: Capacity of shared-secret key agreement over GHZ quantum networks
entry.summary: The Capacity of Conference Key Agreement over GHZ Networks arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper studies how K users sharing independent GHZ states, each held by a subset of users, can agree on a common secret key using local operations and public classical communication. It shows that the conference key capacity equals the key capacity of the classical source obtained by measuring every GHZ state first. This holds even when users keep quantum memory and communicate over many rounds. The capacity also equals the GHZ distillation capacity. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show conference key capacity over GHZ networks equals the classical source key capacity after measuring, so measuring first is optimal.

entry.title: When the entanglement-assisted quantum Singleton bound holds for linear stabilizer codes, and how far it can fail
entry.summary: Validity and maximum violation of the entanglement-assisted quantum Singleton bound for linear stabilizer codes arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper examines whether linear entanglement-assisted stabilizer codes satisfy the entanglement-assisted quantum Singleton bound of Brun, Devetak and Hsieh, which estimates how many pre-shared entangled pairs a code needs. The answer depends on how many qudits, together with the receiver's halves of the pairs, recover the logical qudits. The authors determine when the bound holds, and when it fails, the maximum violation is tied to lengths of classical MDS codes. Apart from cited MDS lengths, the proofs are formalized in the Lean proof assistant. ★★★★ Notable: The authors characterize when the entanglement-assisted quantum Singleton bound holds for linear stabilizer codes and its maximum violation, tied to classical MDS code lengths.

entry.title: Limits of adaptive variational quantum algorithms for lattice field theories in 2+1 dimensions
entry.summary: Prospects and limitations of adaptive variational quantum algorithms for lattice field theories: a case study in 2+1 dimensions arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies whether the ADAPT-VQE algorithm, previously used for lattice gauge theories in 1+1 dimensions, extends to higher dimensions. The authors identify two limitations: with real qubit Hamiltonians and initial states, all real-valued pool operators have zero gradients and are never selected, and the algorithm can converge to excited states. Applying it to free Wilson fermions in 2+1 dimensions, they show both problems occur. Adding charge conjugation symmetry to the operator pool and combining pools with suitable initial states recovers the ground and first excited states across the full mass range.

entry.title: Anomalies and the Berry Phase: From the π⁰ Decay to the Fermion Vacuum Geometry
entry.summary: Anomalies and the Berry Phase: From π⁰→γγ to the geometry of the fermion vacuum arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This review traces the chiral anomaly historically, from the π⁰→γγ puzzle and the work of Adler, Bell and Jackiw to the Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) term. It describes how the WZW term was motivated from quantum chromodynamics in 1983–85. The paper argues that the universal phase of the fermion determinant is the WZW term and can be understood as a Berry phase, with the 1+1 dimensional connection written in Euler angles exhibiting a Dirac monopole.

entry.title: Growing alpha-phase tantalum on sapphire at room temperature using an ultrathin titanium seed layer
entry.summary: Robust growth of α-tantalum on sapphire at room temperature using atomically thin titanium seed layer arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents a room-temperature method for growing alpha-phase tantalum (Ta) films on sapphire substrates using an ultrathin titanium (Ti) seed layer, which widens the usable deposition parameter range. The authors compare these films with Ta grown at high temperature without a seed layer and at room temperature with a niobium (Nb) seed layer, using structural and surface characterization and coplanar-waveguide resonators measured in the quantum regime. The resulting two-level-system-limited quality factors are comparable to state-of-the-art Ta-on-sapphire resonators with similar geometries. The study also finds that high-temperature growth and extended buffered-oxide etch treatment introduce additional temperature-activated loss.

entry.title: Finite-temperature superradiant criticality and thermal emission in the open Dicke model
entry.summary: Finite-Temperature Superradiant Criticality and Thermal Emission in the Open Dicke Model arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies the open Dicke model near its superradiant phase transition at finite temperature, with the cavity mode and atomic ensemble coupled to separate reservoirs at no restriction on coupling strength. For a broad class of spectral densities, the reservoirs leave the temperature-dependent critical coupling unchanged, but the polariton becomes overdamped in a finite range of couplings around it. The authors derive reflection and thermal emission spectra for arbitrary parameters in both the normal and superradiant phases. They also identify conditions under which the system acts as both a perfect absorber and a perfect emitter at specific frequencies.

entry.title: Sorting photon pairs by measured variables to estimate key rates in hyperentangled quantum key distribution
entry.summary: Class-resolved sifting for quantum key distribution with photon pairs hyperentangled in polarization and transverse spatial variables arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper proposes class-resolved sifting for quantum key distribution with photon pairs entangled in both polarization and transverse spatial variables. Each detected pair is assigned to a class based on which degrees of freedom were measured in compatible bases, and error and key rates are estimated separately for each class. Applied to previously reported data from a two-crystal down-conversion source, the method reproduces the key yield of independent sifting and tests cross-dependencies between the two variables. The paper also compares this hyperentangled approach with a single 4-dimensional system measured in two mutually unbiased bases, which yields the same key per detected pair but differs in tensor-product structure.

entry.title: Polynomial master equations for open quantum systems and their critical solutions
entry.summary: Polynomial Master Equations of Open Quantum Systems and an Analysis on the Critical Solutions arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper studies non-Markovian dynamics of open quantum systems, which generally cannot be described by first-order differential equations. It proposes a locally deterministic interpretation and derives non-Markovian linear differential equations associated with higher-order matrix polynomials. The method is illustrated with exact analyses of a two-qubit system and an infinite-dimensional system with an unbounded Hamiltonian. The authors also analyze critical parameters where the system dynamics change qualitatively.

entry.title: Iterative Petz Protocols for Quantum State Recovery: A method that repeatedly updates its reference state to reverse quantum noise
entry.summary: Iterative Petz Protocols for Quantum State Recovery arXiv · Nov 25, 2026Noise is unavoidable in quantum systems, so approximately reversing it is a central challenge. The paper introduces the iterative Petz recovery (IPR) protocol, which starts from an unbiased reference state and uses each recovered output to build the Petz map for the next iteration. The authors establish the protocol's stability and give a tomography-assisted finite-copy implementation with explicit control of error propagation and fidelity loss. For qubit depolarizing noise and single-axis Pauli noise they derive exact fidelity recurrences, and they benchmark finite-copy IPR against measure-and-prepare strategies, revealing finite-resource tradeoffs.

entry.title: Entanglement asymmetry and quantum Mpemba effect in non-uniform quenches
entry.summary: Entanglement Asymmetry and the Quantum Mpemba Effect in Inhomogeneous Quenches arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies a spin-1/2 XX chain whose two halves start in tilted ferromagnetic states with different tilt angles. The authors combine generalized hydrodynamics and the quasiparticle picture with exact fermionic correlation-matrix calculations to track how entanglement asymmetry evolves. The two approaches agree well for generic initial configurations, and the quantum Mpemba effect is observed, where states with stronger initial symmetry breaking restore symmetry faster. The effect depends on subsystem position, with interface-straddling subsystems showing multiple crossings or none.

entry.title: Trotterized hybrid qubit-boson circuit simulation of the Jaynes-Cummings-Hubbard model
entry.summary: Trotterized hybrid qubit-boson simulation of the Jaynes-Cummings-Hubbard model arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper designs a Trotterized quantum circuit to simulate real-time dynamics of the Jaynes-Cummings-Hubbard model, which describes light-matter interaction in coupled optical cavities. Using Bosonic Qiskit with a Matrix Product State backend, the authors simulate single-polariton transport and benchmark site occupations against exact diagonalization. They extend the study to the two-excitation sector under a hard-core photon constraint and examine how bipartite entanglement entropy depends on inter-cavity photon-hopping strength.

entry.title: Perturbative unitarity limits on coupling constants from qubit entanglement in scalar scattering and QED
entry.summary: Perturbative unitarity bounds from qubit entanglement in scalar scattering and QED arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper analyzes, within the perturbative S-matrix framework for relativistic 2→2 scattering, the quantum channels obtained by tracing out momentum from the scattered state. It considers two qubit-based scenarios, flavored scalar contact interactions and QED, with initial-state leptons of transverse polarization. The entanglement of the qubits is computed via concurrence, and its maximal allowed value is used to derive perturbativity upper bounds on coupling constants.

entry.title: Using SU(2) symmetry to prepare matrix product states efficiently on quantum computers
entry.summary: Exploiting SU(2) Symmetry for Efficient Quantum State Preparation of Matrix Product States arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper proposes a way to compile matrix product states, obtained classically with the density matrix renormalization group, into fault-tolerant quantum circuits by exploiting non-Abelian SU(2) spin symmetry. Using the Wigner-Eckart theorem, only the reduced tensors need generic unitary synthesis, while the magnetic structure is restored through Clebsch-Gordan transformations. Using Toffoli count as the main cost metric, the method is benchmarked on the one-dimensional Hubbard model, quasi-one-dimensional Hubbard geometries, and Anderson impurity models. It reduces the Toffoli cost roughly threefold relative to U(1)-adapted compilation and by more than an order of magnitude relative to the standard dense method.

entry.title: Exact solution of a one-dimensional boson-fermion mixture along a special parameter line
entry.summary: Exact solution of the Bose-Fermi mixture along the unnesting line arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies a one-dimensional mixture of bosons and fermions with contact repulsive interactions, a model that can be solved exactly by nested Bethe ansatz. The authors simplify the solution along a special line where the Bethe-ansatz equations can be unnested, and express it through known solutions of the Lieb-Liniger and Yang-Gaudin models. They obtain explicit analytical results for the ground-state energy, excitation velocities and Drude weights at weak and strong interactions.

entry.title: Programmable multipartite entanglement analogues in classical electromagnetic waves
entry.summary: Programmable multipartite entanglement analogues arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents a spatiotemporal metasurface that reconfigures which state spaces, such as polarization, frequency, and orbital angular momentum, are coherently linked in classical electromagnetic fields. The authors realize Bell-like and GHZ-like state families from bipartite to five-partite order and can swap constituents while keeping the order fixed. They report that the five-partite state is the highest multipartite order experimentally realized in classical electromagnetic fields.

entry.title: Classical sampling of verifiable graph-state quantum advantage experiments
entry.summary: Classical sampling of verifiable graph-state quantum advantage experiments arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper examines a proposed quantum advantage experiment that uses graph states with built-in error detection so that results can be verified without simulation. The authors show that the two instances posted on IBM hardware can be classically sampled on eight GPUs. The 70-qubit instance is sampled from the ideal output distribution, and the 64-qubit instance with 314 T gates reaches a certified fidelity of at least 0.908, versus 0.349 for the hardware. The authors argue that T gates must sit where error detection cannot see them, which pushes them to the circuit's end and keeps classical cost low.

entry.title: Loss and recovery of conformality in Anderson localization: a phenomenological theory of high-dimensional transitions
entry.summary: Conformality lost in Anderson localization in infinite dimensions, and regained in finite dimensions: a phenomenological theory of the Anderson transition in high dimensions arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies Anderson localization as the number of spatial dimensions goes to infinity. It argues that recent work fits a scenario called conformality lost, in which two renormalization group fixed points collide and become complex. In this picture, a two-parameter scaling flow of the Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless type controls the theory's observables. The authors also expand the renormalization group equations in 1/d, obtaining phenomenological equations that fit numerical results for dimensions d ≳ 4.

entry.title: Krylov dynamics of deformed oscillator chains: localization, ballistic spreading, and indeterminacy
entry.summary: Krylov dynamics of deformed oscillator chains: localization, ballistic spreading, and indeterminacy arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper studies Krylov chains generated by a two-parameter (p,q)-deformed oscillator, mapping quantum dynamics to a quantum walk whose hopping amplitudes are Lanczos coefficients. Depending on the deformation parameters, spread complexity stays bounded, grows ballistically, or grows as t². When the moment problem is indeterminate, complexity is defined only after a boundary condition at infinite Krylov index is specified.

entry.title: Observation of programmable spatiotemporal quantum-inspired bits
entry.summary: Observation of programmable spatiotemporal quantum-inspired bits arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This study observes programmable spatiotemporal quantum-inspired bits in a space-time metasurface. Coherent synthesis of four discrete responses per polarization channel yields two-component states with the geometry of a pure quantum bit. Paired spatial and temporal codes arrange these states into prescribed trajectories, reconfigurable Stokes skyrmions, and distinct polarizations across 48 resolved harmonic orders, providing a physical basis for information carriers that use geometric paths and spectral states.

entry.title: Probing a rung-Mott insulator in bosonic two-leg ladders
entry.summary: Probing the Rung-Mott Insulator in Bosonic Two-Leg Ladders arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This study uses ultracold bosonic atoms in strongly interacting two-leg ladders near half-filling to identify a rung-Mott insulating (RMI) phase through site-resolved measurements of rung occupation. The excitation spectrum is probed by lattice modulation spectroscopy and interpreted with numerical simulations that include driven dynamics, coupling to multiple excited states, and energy offsets. The phase is characterized by its incompressibility, examined through site-resolved analysis of densities and chemical potentials.

entry.title: Electrons in a twisted hard-wall cylinder: time-reversal degeneracy and twist-induced transitions
entry.summary: Electrons in a hard-wall cylinder with helicoidal metric: time-reversal pairing, cubic anticrossings, and twist-activated dipole transitions arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper studies the scalar Schrödinger equation in a helicoidal metric with Dirichlet hard walls closing the axial direction. In a rotationally symmetric spinless cavity, time reversal makes levels with azimuthal numbers m and -m exactly degenerate. It gives an exact variational representation and analyzes an avoided crossing at a radial-axial resonance, along with a transverse dipole transition that gains oscillator strength from the twist.

entry.title: Detecting and Reconstructing Hidden Correlations in Gaussian Light
entry.summary: Witnessing Gaussian Coexistence and Correlation-Ellipse Tomography arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies how to detect Gaussian coexistence, where covariance and pseudocovariance are present together between two zero-mean Gaussian light modes. The authors show that second- and third-order intensity moments cannot detect it, while a balanced fourth-order residual gives a necessary and sufficient witness. Adding an independent correlated thermal probe lets the two correlation strengths be identified separately, and a coherent reference in one arm gives the relative phase via third-order correlation. Together these measurements reconstruct the correlation ellipse and its Poincaré-sphere coordinates.

entry.title: Phase information and measurement in the stochastic-quantum correspondence, explained
entry.summary: Phase information and measurement in the Stochastic--Quantum correspondence arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies the stochastic-quantum correspondence, which links general stochastic processes to quantum dynamics through quantum lifts on a Hilbert space. It introduces context-dependent families of stochastic processes and shows that their continuation probabilities encode the predictive information held in off-diagonal terms. The authors also explain how quantum measurement fits this view, with active continuations making basis-dependent probabilities appear as configuration probabilities.

entry.title: Quantum optimization beyond qubit count using low-energy subspace sampling
entry.summary: Quantum optimization beyond qubit count by low-energy subspace sampling arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper introduces Quantum Subspace Sampling Descent (QSSD), an iterative heuristic that separates the number of problem variables from the number of qubits. It uses a fixed-angle Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm as a low-energy sampler and was tested on IBM Heron and Nighthawk devices with up to 152 qubits. On a 10000-variable instance, QSSD reached an approximation ratio above 0.95 with 100 circuit executions, though it does not yet match the best classical baseline.

entry.title: Controlled teleportation of an unknown qutrit and how much control it gives
entry.summary: Controlled teleportation of an unknown qutrit and its control power arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper proposes a controlled quantum teleportation protocol for an arbitrary unknown three-level quantum state, using a non-maximally entangled channel. A controller holds a qubit, while the sender and receiver each hold a four-level particle. With an auxiliary qubit, the receiver can probabilistically recover the input state with unit fidelity. The authors derive the overall success probability and define the controller's influence as the difference in optimal average teleportation fidelity with and without the controller's cooperation.

entry.title: Infinite-dimensional extended Bloch representation: a mathematical framework for quantum mechanics
entry.summary: The infinite-dimensional extended Bloch representation arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies the extended Bloch representation (EBR) of quantum mechanics when the number of measurement outcomes tends to infinity. Renormalization, with the generalized Bloch ball radius growing like N, makes the distances from measurement interactions to the simplex facets independent exponential random variables. The authors also describe the limiting structure for both pure point and continuous spectra.

entry.title: When Randomness Hides Quantum Simulation Errors: How Input-State Statistics Affect Trotter Error Visibility
entry.summary: When Randomness Hides Quantum Simulation Errors arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies how errors in measured observables from Trotter formulas, which approximate quantum dynamics in discrete steps, depend on the randomness of the input states. It shows that the mean absolute observable-error bound for state 2-designs can be exponentially smaller in qubit number than the tight bound for state 1-designs. The authors use the frame potential to quantify deviations from random-state statistics and derive a sufficient pth-order Trotter number of O(T^{1+3/(4p)}) for a Hamiltonian trajectory whose frame potential decays as 1/T.

entry.title: Perfect state transfer on special tree graphs under Grover walks
entry.summary: Perfect state transfer in Grover walks on generalized Bethe trees arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies whether generalized Bethe trees, a family of tree graphs, allow perfect state transfer between vertex states in Grover walks. The authors fully classify which such trees exhibit this behavior. They show it occurs exactly when the tree is a path or a uniform subdivision of B(2,3) or B(1,2,3). The paper also identifies all transferring vertex pairs and their minimum transfer times.

entry.title: Machine learning method for reducing quantum noise in bound-state simulations
entry.summary: Machine Learning-Based Quantum Error Mitigation for Bound-State Simulations arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper introduces a machine learning quantum error mitigation framework that uses residual learning with convex projection so reconstructed density matrices are physically valid. The authors compare different training datasets and regression models using Haar-random and VQE ansatz states. The method was tested on IBM quantum hardware for three- and four-qubit simulations of Λ-deuteron and Λ-α hypernuclear systems. Reported ground-state energies approach ideal values, with state fidelities of 0.995 to 0.999.

entry.title: Spin relaxation and coherence times of silicon vacancies in 4H-SiC
entry.summary: Electron spin relaxation and coherence times of silicon vacancies in 4H-SiC arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies electron spins of silicon vacancy centers (V1 and V2) in 4H silicon carbide between 80 and 300 K, using electron paramagnetic resonance. It reports spin concentrations for V1, V2 and an unidentified defect X, and compares coherence and relaxation times on central and satellite spectral lines. Satellite transitions show longer T1 and T2, with maxima of 42.8 ms and 0.708 ms at 80 K. The authors attribute decoherence mainly to nuclear and electron spin diffusion.

entry.title: Preparing thermal states with shallow quantum circuits
entry.summary: Thermal state preparation with shallow quantum circuits arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper introduces PP-VarQITE, which combines Pauli propagation with variational quantum imaginary-time evolution to determine circuit parameters entirely classically, encoding target temperatures in the angles of a fixed circuit. Numerical studies of Ising and frustrated Heisenberg models recover low-temperature energies and correlations using up to 100 qubits. The authors also prepare a 48-site frustrated chain and a 7×7 Ising lattice on the Quantinuum Helios trapped-ion processor.

entry.title: Quantum coherence and basis-dependent correlations: structural conditions for bipartite states
entry.summary: Quantum Coherence and Basis-Dependent Correlations in Quantum Systems arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies how quantum coherence and quantum correlations relate, focusing on which bipartite states have equal coherence in the global and reduced states. Using the Tsallis relative entropy coherence measure and a coherence measure based on quantum Fisher information, the authors show that block-diagonal product states have vanishing basis-dependent correlations. In a special case, they establish an equivalence between vanishing basis-dependent correlations and block-diagonal product structure. For two-qubit states under the Fisher-information measure, the condition is a broader block-diagonal-like product structure.

entry.title: Quantum tautochrone effect for photons and atoms
entry.summary: Quantum Tautochrone for photons and atoms arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper extends the classical tautochrone problem, where travel time to a common point is independent of starting position, into quantum physics. It studies photonic waveguide arrays and atomic optical lattices with nonuniform couplings, where particles launched from different sites converge simultaneously to a common site. Using higher-order correlation functions, the authors show the effect holds for both bosons and fermions. Bosons converge onto the same site, while fermions gather at neighboring sites due to Pauli exclusion.

entry.title: Dynamic scaling in quantum Ising systems under periodic driving
entry.summary: Dynamic scaling behaviors induced by periodic drivings at continuous Ising quantum transitions arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies out-of-equilibrium scaling behavior in zero-temperature quantum many-body systems near continuous quantum phase transitions, induced by periodic driving. It examines a quantum Ising chain under periodic longitudinal fields and a Kitaev fermionic wire with periodically driven chemical potentials, which is equivalent to an Ising chain with a periodic transverse field. Using a renormalization-group framework, the authors develop a dynamic scaling theory for finite-size systems and the thermodynamic limit, distinguishing drivings that break the global Z2 symmetry from those that preserve it. Numerical simulations verify the theory for smooth single-frequency and square-wave drivings.

entry.title: A quantum-inspired spiking autoencoder for spotting unusual particle collisions at the LHC
entry.summary: A quantum-inspired spiking variational autoencoder for robust anomaly detection at the LHC arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper introduces the quantum-inspired spiking variational autoencoder (QSVAE), built on a quantum-inspired leaky integrate-and-fire (QLIF) neuron, and describes it as the first fully spiking variational autoencoder. It is designed for model-agnostic anomaly detection in di-jet latent spaces from the Large Hadron Collider. The neuron is reformulated from a measurement-based circuit into a differentiable computational unit and benchmarked against classical, spiking, and quantum models. Under noise perturbations, the QLIF network retains 0.95 of its clean accuracy, while twelve classical models retain only 0.74 to 0.85.

entry.title: Rydberg constraint ensembles for non-native binary optimization
entry.summary: Rydberg Constraint Ensembles for Nonnative Binary Optimization arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper expands the finite penalties produced by Rydberg blockade into a weighted ensemble of exclusion graphs whose full ensemble preserves the ground energy. The interactions remaining on each graph set its local detunings. In simulations of two coupled squares, the authors report that on 32 held-out twelve-site targets the average simulated probability of recovering a ground state in 128 shots is 69.82% with residual detunings versus 24.31% with a tuned uniform pulse.

entry.title: Improving quantum oblivious transfer by adding zero-knowledge proofs
entry.summary: Improving Quantum Oblivious Transfer using Zero-Knowledge Proofs arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper proposes enhancing quantum oblivious transfer protocols with zero-knowledge proofs, in which the receiver proves it honestly followed key protocol steps without revealing extra information to the sender. The authors report that this gives a tighter security bound against malicious receivers, cutting the required quantum communication by one to two orders of magnitude for a fixed security target. They also note a substantial computational overhead and introduce a tunable variant that trades off efficiency against that overhead.

entry.title: Composition rules in deriving quantum mechanics from axioms
entry.summary: The role of composition rules in an axiomatic derivation of quantum mechanics arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper examines an information-theoretic axiomatization of quantum mechanics that relies on local discriminability and purification axioms for compound systems. The authors argue that the tensor product structure these axioms assume should be grounded in explicit formal composition rules for embedding local effects and reducing joint states. They formally define local measurements, state axioms of local discrimination, and rewrite the purification axioms in a weaker form. The paper also discusses multipartite composition axioms and associativity.

entry.title: Faster ground-state search for neural quantum states using implicit time steps
entry.summary: Augmented Imaginary-Time Evolution of Neural Quantum States with Implicit Time Steps arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper addresses finding ground states of quantum many-body systems with neural quantum states optimized by imaginary-time evolution. The authors combine an implicit Euler step with Galerkin projection to derive an implicit stochastic reconfiguration scheme that allows large, stable steps. They then build an implicit version of augmented imaginary-time evolution (AITE) and show its acceleration holds under variational projection and finite-step integration, with asymptotically quadratic convergence of the energy error.

entry.title: Magnetometry and slow light in PT-symmetric cavity optomechanics
entry.summary: Magnetometry and slow light in PT-symmetric cavity optomechanics arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies second-order sideband generation and tunable slow and fast light in a parity-time (PT)-symmetric cavity optomechanical system, and proposes an enhanced magnetometer scheme. The PT-symmetric structure, an external magnetic field, and photon tunneling strength flexibly control the sideband efficiency and the broadening and switching of slow-fast light propagation. In the PT-symmetry-protected phases, the authors report a theoretical magnetometer sensitivity at the picotesla level.

entry.title: Quantum entanglement between distant magnet spins forms a d-wave clover pattern
entry.summary: Entanglement between distant spins in a polarized magnet forms a d-wave clover arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper studies how spin-orbit coupling in a polarized magnet creates virtual spin-flip pairs that entangle distant spins. For a spin-1/2 square-lattice ferromagnet, it proves at leading order a d-wave inverse-square law and a clover-shaped entangled region, exact even without the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya term. The authors also state that four qubits can test the d-wave signs at current error rates.

entry.title: Transfer tensor description of periodically driven, inhomogeneous quantum systems
entry.summary: Transfer tensor description of driven inhomogeneous quantum systems arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The transfer tensor method (TTM) predicts how open quantum systems evolve using short-time trajectories, encoding memory effects in a set of transfer tensors. This paper extends the method to periodically driven systems that lack time-translational invariance, using a two-time transfer tensor hierarchy. It compares sub-stroboscopic sampling with averaging over the driving phase. The authors apply the framework to an inhomogeneously broadened two-level ensemble driven beyond the rotating-wave approximation and to a driven tight-binding chain at the Dunlap–Kenkre condition, comparing their memory effects and localization behavior.

entry.title: Light-controlled transverse Wigner ordering in attosecond electron beams
entry.summary: Toward light-controlled transverse Wigner ordering in attosecond electron beams arXiv · Nov 24, 2026Kinetic fluctuations and space-charge expansion disrupt Wigner ordering in free-electron beams. The paper proposes a laser-driven method combining PINEM attosecond bunching, synchronized magnetic focusing, and spatial preconditioning to create transient, substrate-free Wigner ordering. Classical relaxation and zero-temperature fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo benchmarks show that sixfold order survives quantum fluctuations from 1 T to sub-Tesla fields, defining ultrafast preparation targets.

entry.title: Removing measurement incompatibility in quantum multiparameter estimation using antiparallel probes
entry.summary: Eliminating Incompatibility in Quantum Multiparameter Estimation with Antiparallel Probes arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper studies why measuring several quantum parameters at once is limited by measurement incompatibility, which prevents the SLD Cramér-Rao bound from being reached. The authors show that antiparallel probe configurations can reach this bound without losing quantum Fisher information, provided the parameter encoding preserves those configurations, giving a metrological advantage. For qubit probes, this advantage exists if and only if the encoding channel is unital.

entry.title: A Koashi–Imoto criterion for when Holevo-rate quantum compression is achievable
entry.summary: A Koashi--Imoto Criterion for Holevo-Rate Visible Compression arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper studies a finite memoryless quantum source whose encoder knows the sequence of classical labels, and determines when the Holevo rate can be achieved with shared classical randomness and no shared entanglement. The criterion uses the maximal Koashi–Imoto decomposition of the signal ensemble: the rate is achievable exactly when each signal is pure on the quantum part of every sector it occupies. For qubits this means all signals are pure or commute pairwise.

entry.title: Quantum-inspired tensor train spectral solver for high-resolution PDEs with non-periodic boundaries
entry.summary: Quantum-Inspired Tensor Train Spectral Solver for High-Resolution PDEs with Non-Periodic Boundary Conditions arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces superfast cosine and sine transforms, extending tensor train spectral methods to homogeneous Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions. Both transforms are derived from a shared TT operator representation, and their TT ranks are shown to be bounded by 6r_S, independent of discretization order. For Rayleigh-Bénard convection, spectral pressure projection gives up to a 7-fold speedup in the Poisson solve with comparable accuracy. For three-dimensional computational homogenization, the approach achieves a 2-6-fold speedup and a 4-7-fold memory reduction compared with an existing TT-based method.

entry.title: Quantum kernels on breast data: whether claimed advantages hold up
entry.summary: Quantum kernels on breast data: concentration, surrogates, and two ways an advantage gets manufactured arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper examines claimed quantum-kernel advantages on breast data using fully classical simulations with no quantum component in inference. It compares the quantum kernel against many classical comparators and accounts for model selection effects. All three main benchmarks are negative, and the apparent advantage is shown to come from comparator choice and seed selection.

entry.title: Error-mitigation method to recover order-finding results from noisy quantum circuits
entry.summary: Theory-Informed Quantum Error Mitigation for Shor Order Finding with Fourier Neural Operators arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper proposes a theory-informed quantum error mitigation method for recovering the correct result of Shor order finding from noisy measurement distributions. The authors model how circuit errors shift, broaden, or weaken peaks, use these models to generate synthetic training data, and design a Fourier neural operator with a learned gain. On 1,351 simulated test cases, exact order recovery rose from 19% to 34% and median Jensen-Shannon divergence fell from 0.64 to 0.32. On 101 Mersenne rotation circuits run on five IBM quantum processors, correct order estimates increased from 35 to 53.

entry.title: Streaming portfolio optimization using Pauli Correlation Encoding for large asset universes
entry.summary: Large-Scale Streaming Portfolio Optimization with Pauli Correlation Encoding arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies portfolio selection across large asset universes using Pauli Correlation Encoding (PCE), which represents the clustering problem with far fewer qubits than assets. The authors extend an earlier static test to a streaming setting where correlations and portfolios are re-estimated on a rolling basis, introducing PCE and a joint multi-cut variant, dPCE. Both streaming methods outperform a Buy & Hold baseline, and PCE loses markedly less during a market downturn. The authors find PCE more practical at scale and identify which operational choices, such as rebalancing cadence and transaction-cost awareness, matter most.

entry.title: Quantum community detection for analyzing data, including selecting features and grouping items.
entry.summary: Quantum Community Detection for Data Analysis arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies quantum spectral community detection, such as the deteQt algorithm based on the modularity matrix, for feature selection and clustering. The authors extend deteQt to multiple communities through recursive bisection and propose projeQt, which applies a spectral filter via quantum singular value transformation to extract several communities at once. On MNIST, both pipelines select informative pixels and classify images by clustering, and perform competitively with standard community detectors.

entry.title: Quantum capacity when codes are restricted to incoherent operations
entry.summary: Quantum Capacity with Incoherent Codes arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper studies quantum channel capacity when the encoder is limited to incoherent operations. It shows that arbitrarily weak depolarizing noise reduces the quantum capacity to zero in this setting. It gives a single-letter formula for the capacity with incoherent encoding and shows that imposing incoherent decoding reduces capacity by at most a factor of two, which is optimal. The authors also evaluate these capacities for multiqubit Pauli channels.

entry.title: Photon number correlations in harmonics driven by classical and quantum light
entry.summary: Photon number correlations in harmonics driven with classical and quantum light arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper compares low-photon-number perturbative harmonic generation driven by classical light and by bright squeezed vacuum. The squeezed vacuum source produces strong auto- and cross-correlations in the harmonic spectrum. Using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and heralding measurements, the authors show that the cross-correlations are fully classical and arise from common fluctuations of the driving field.

entry.title: QDMin: Quantum Search for Energy Minima in Nuclear Shape Landscapes
entry.summary: QDMin: Coherent Quantum Minimum Finding over Parametrized Many-Body Hamiltonians arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents QDMin, a method for locating the minimum of a nuclear collective energy landscape. It searches a parameterized Hamiltonian family using a coherent collective-coordinate register and an on-demand ground-energy threshold oracle, avoiding point-by-point construction of the landscape. The method is implemented for a schematic pairing-plus-multipole model, with calculations at four points and on a 4×4 quadrupole–octupole grid.

entry.title: Dissipation dilution boosts SiV coupling to diamond nanomechanical beams
entry.summary: Enhanced SiV-phonon coupling in dissipation-diluted diamond nanomechanics arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper experimentally studies a tensioned diamond nanobeam platform where strain couples negatively charged silicon vacancy centers to a mechanical resonator. By monitoring the SiVs' optical response, the authors observe that dynamical strain localizes near the clamps under static strain. This enhances both SiV-mechanical coupling and mechanical coherence, and yields a strain sensitivity with much better accuracy than prior literature values.

entry.title: Optimizing a Quantum Battery with Counterdiabatic Driving
entry.summary: Geodesic Efficiency of Counterdiabatic Charging in a Quantum Battery arXiv · Oct 23, 2026This paper studies how a quantum battery charges within an open quantum framework, using a driven qubit as the charger and an ancilla as a controllable switch. It uses an adiabatic protocol for lossless energy transfer and adds a counterdiabatic control field to suppress unwanted transitions and speed up charging. The authors report that charging efficiency improves under adiabatic evolution with stable, non-oscillatory behavior, and they identify an optimal operation time.

entry.title: Quantum sampling for gradient-based simulation optimization beyond classical minimax rates
entry.summary: Beyond Classical Minimax Rates: Quantum Sampling in Gradient-Based Simulation Optimization arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies gradient-based search for convex simulation optimization problems, where gradients are estimated from noisy outputs. The authors apply quantum mean estimation to paired finite differences, increasing estimation accuracy as perturbations shrink, which improves the convergence rate from the classical O(N^{-2/3}) to O(N^{-4/3}). They also give rates for coupled nearby evaluations and prove matching lower bounds showing these accuracy exponents are minimax optimal for fixed decision dimension. ★★★★ Notable: The authors apply quantum mean estimation to paired finite differences, improving the convergence exponent and reporting matching minimax lower bounds for simulation optimization.

entry.title: Coherent conversion between mesons and baryons in a cold-atom non-Abelian lattice gauge simulator
entry.summary: Coherent meson-baryon conversion in a cold-atom non-Abelian lattice gauge simulator arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper realizes a non-Abelian lattice gauge model with dynamical matter in an analog cold-atom simulator and observes its hadronic dynamics with site- and spin-resolved quantum gas microscopy. It uses two hyperfine states and site occupations of 87Rb atoms to encode both matter and gauge fields, and tailors resonant tunneling in a spin-dependent optical superlattice to implement a truncated one-dimensional SU(2) quantum link model. Slow mass ramps reveal coherent oscillations between mesons and baryon-antibaryon pairs, with the conversion efficiency characterized against mass, gauge coupling and net baryon density. ★★★★ Notable: The authors realize a non-Abelian lattice gauge model in cold atoms and report coherent meson-baryon oscillations observed with quantum gas microscopy.

entry.title: Neural decoder for logical Clifford circuits built from transversal gates
entry.summary: Neural Decoding of Logical Clifford Circuits with Transversal Gates arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper presents Duet, a neural decoder for logical Clifford circuits that use transversal gates, which builds in known gate structure and how logical outcomes propagate, learning only which errors occurred. On circuits with 2 to 4 blocks and up to 16 layers, Duet alone beats matching at every distance, and paired with the Tesseract search decoder it fails 44 times less often than LoMatching at distance 9. The method takes 2.4 to 121.7 microseconds per layer. ★★★★ Notable: The authors embed known error propagation and linear logical outcome flips into a neural decoder paired with Tesseract; the abstract reports much lower failure rates than matching and LoMatching on ra

entry.title: Spinal reflected entropy reveals logical magic
entry.summary: Spinal reflected entropy reveals logical magic arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper links quantum entanglement and quantum magic in the toric code. It introduces spinal reflected entropy, which connects the stabilizer Rényi entropy of the stored logical state to entanglement. The quantity obeys an area law with a topological correction, and the result extends to higher-genus surfaces and general two-dimensional topological stabilizer codes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors link logical magic to a geometric reflected-entropy quantity, give an analytic relation on the torus, and extend it to higher-genus surfaces and general topological stabilizer codes.

entry.title: Locality from Nonlocality: Relocalizing Symmetries and Gauging Lattice Dirac Fermions
entry.summary: Locality from Nonlocality: Symmetry Relocalization and Gauging of Lattice Dirac Fermions arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper shows that certain exact nonlocal compact symmetries of free lattice Dirac fermions can be made onsite through nonlocal canonical transformations while preserving enough Hamiltonian locality to allow gauging. It studies this symmetry relocalization in one, two, and three dimensions, relating gauge locality to lattice structure, topology, and anomalies. The work also covers bosonization, duality, and non-Abelian extensions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a nonlocal canonical transformation relocalizing compact symmetries in 1D, 2D, and 3D, with norm-resolvent bounds and no-go theorems.

entry.title: QuOptLab: An AI agent that runs and refines quantum optics experiments
entry.summary: QuOptLab: Advancing Quantum Optics Experiments with an AI Agent arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper builds a simulated quantum optics laboratory with instruments, a robotic arm, and cameras, and connects it to an AI agent called QuOptLab. The agent carries out experiments, analyzes results, and iteratively refines experimental designs. It is tested on thin-film thickness measurement in free-space optics and edge-coupler design in integrated photonics.

entry.title: Schur saturation and Clifford limits in qudit CSS codes (a study showing some quantum codes pass orthogonality tests yet lack non-Clifford gates)
entry.summary: Schur saturation and the Clifford ceiling in qudit CSS codes arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper studies symmetric spectral CSS codes built from character evaluation on a finite abelian group. It shows that the dual code satisfies a Schur saturation identity, which kills local polynomial phases of degree three and above. A complete gate-group classification indicates that strictly CSS-preserving local-diagonal transversal gates lie at level two or below of the Clifford hierarchy, and this is verified on the instance [[64,56,3]]_5.

entry.title: Simulating quantum correlations with few shared random labels and a hybrid source
entry.summary: Hybrid correlation generation with finite shared randomness arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper studies how finite shared randomness can reduce reliance on a prescribed two-qubit source in a hybrid model, reproducing joint outcome distributions of fixed binary measurements exactly. It shows eight labels suffice to preserve all feasible interface-choice probability pairs and that this bound is tight. For Werner states with identical orthogonal measurement pairs, exact minimum source costs are obtained for every label budget.

entry.title: A machine learning method for scaling holographic quantum circuits
entry.summary: A machine learning architecture for scaling of holographic quantum circuits arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper presents an architecture and workflow for learning and generalizing the structure and parameters of holographic quantum circuits (HQCs), quantum analogs of tensor networks. HQCs use mid-circuit measurements and resets on physical qubits coupled to persistent ancilla qubits, so their outcomes become correlated. The method extrapolates gate sequences and rotation angles learned from a set of HQCs to longer or more expressive circuits. The authors demonstrate the approach on an analytically solvable vector-valued generalization of the W state.

entry.title: Controlling electron decoherence in a twisted helical structure via chirality
entry.summary: Geometric Control of Electronic Decoherence in a Chiral Spin-Orbit Coupled Helix arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper uses a chiral helix as a model to study how electronic decoherence changes with helical twist within the Born-Markov regime. It finds that moderate to strong spin-orbit coupling between next-nearest-neighbor sites makes the decoherence rate strongly depend on chirality. Spatial and temporal correlations in local environmental fluctuations also strongly affect this behavior, suggesting chirality as a tunable design parameter for quantum engineering.

entry.title: A colored view of anyons and parastatistics
entry.summary: A colored look at anyons and parastatistics arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper reviews recent progress on color Lie (super)algebras, which Rittenberg and Wyler introduced in 1978 as generalizations of ordinary Lie (super)algebras. The color framework describes two types of parastatistics: paraparticles, exchanged via the permutation group in any spatial dimension, and anyons, exchanged via the braid group in up to two spatial dimensions. The paper aims to offer a new colored perspective on parastatistics and braid statistics.

entry.title: From outcome exclusion to measurement simulation
entry.summary: From outcome exclusion to measurement simulation arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper develops a quantitative framework for measurement outcome exclusion, which has been less studied than quantum state exclusion. It gives necessary and sufficient criteria for simulating one measurement from another using quantum pre-processing and classical post-processing. Algebraic exclusion indices and random exclusion profiles are introduced, and both are shown to be monotone under these processing types.

entry.title: Light Pulses That Hold Their Shape in Modern Fiber Lasers
entry.summary: Temporal Soliton Waves in Modern Fiber Laser Systems arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This chapter surveys temporal soliton waves, which are localized nonlinear pulse structures in modern fiber systems. They arise from balances among dispersion, nonlinearity, gain, loss, spectral filtering, and cavity coupling. The text reviews theory, experimental findings, and methods for generating, characterizing, and controlling these solitons, with emphasis on mode-locked fiber lasers. It covers dissipative solitons, soliton molecules, and dispersion-managed solitons.

entry.title: An exact method for analyzing two- and three-excitation bound states in open quantum systems
entry.summary: Exact approach to double- and triple-excitation bound state in open quantum systems arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies the dynamics of double- and triple-excitation states in interacting quantum emitters coupled to an environment. The authors derive a closed equation that yields the critical condition for these multiple-excitation bound states to emerge and relates it to the single-excitation case. The results indicate that such bound states are universal in open quantum emitter systems and may be used to mediate interactions between emitters.

entry.title: Symmetry rules limiting which many-body correlations shape nonlinear optical responses in Rydberg-EIT media
entry.summary: Symmetry-constrained order hierarchy of connected optical responses in a five-level Rydberg-EIT medium arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies which connected many-body correlations can contribute to nonlinear optical responses in a driven-dissipative Rydberg-EIT model. Using local phase covariance and zero-probe factorization, the authors show that an n-atom connected contribution is forbidden below probe-amplitude order 2n-1. As a result, optical-response coefficients through fifth order involve at most three-atom clusters, without assuming weak interatomic interactions.

entry.title: Probing the internal structure of bound states
entry.summary: Probing the inner structure of bound states arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper uses quantum subspace expansion (QSE) to build composite particle eigenstates and measure how much each added operator type contributes by comparing state fidelities with the full QSE state. Using the scalar meson of the massive Schwinger model as a benchmark, it finds fermion bilinears suffice at large fermion masses, while spatially extended meson-meson operators greatly improve fidelity at small masses. The authors also report that the scalar charge is more sensitive to meson-meson operators than the meson mass, and the parton distribution function becomes asymmetric about momentum fraction 1/2.

entry.title: Parton Physics in the Schwinger Model Using Matrix Product States
entry.summary: Parton Physics in the Schwinger Model from Matrix Product States arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper computes parton distribution functions, light-cone distribution amplitudes, and vector meson decay constants in the Schwinger model directly in Minkowski space, using a Hamiltonian framework. It represents quantum states with matrix product states, whose accuracy is controlled by bond dimension, and quantifies systematic uncertainties by varying and extrapolating lattice spacing, volume, and other parameters. The authors confirm that the computed distributions satisfy the expected normalizations, momentum sum rules, and symmetry properties.

entry.title: Light-cone distributions of vector and scalar mesons in the Schwinger model via tensor networks
entry.summary: Light-cone distributions of vector and scalar bound states in the Schwinger model from tensor networks arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper uses tensor network methods to compute parton distribution functions and light-cone distribution amplitudes for vector and scalar meson bound states in the massive Schwinger model. The two mesons show different light-cone structures: the vector meson has a single-peaked PDF and a symmetric LCDA, while the scalar meson has a double-peaked PDF and an antisymmetric LCDA. For larger fermion masses, the PDFs closely follow the squared LCDAs, and the decay constants approach nonrelativistic model predictions.

entry.title: Phase matching of high-harmonic generation driven by coherent light combined with squeezed vacuum
entry.summary: Phase matching of high-order harmonics driven by a combined coherent and bright squeezed vacuum field arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies phase matching in high-order harmonic generation driven jointly by an intense coherent field and a weak bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) field. It uses a semiclassical ensemble of coherent-field realizations sampled from the Husimi-Q distribution. The authors explain the physical mechanism behind the distinct gas-pressure dependence of odd, even, and half-integer sideband yields seen in an earlier experiment. The BSV-induced perturbation of the electron action phase adds a sub-cycle phase mismatch, so that gas pressure can significantly change sub-cycle burst amplitudes after macroscopic propagation.

entry.title: Scaling limits of time-averaged distributions for symmetric quantum walks on hypercubes
entry.summary: Scaling Limits of Time-averaged Distributions for Symmetric Quantum Walks on Hypercubes arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies continuous-time and discrete-time quantum walks on the hypercube {0,1}^d linked to symmetric random walks whose transition probabilities depend only on Hamming distance, analyzed via the Hamming scheme and Krawtchouk polynomials. For continuous-time walks, the time-averaged Hamming distance distribution is a discrete arcsine law when the eigenvalues are distinct. For discrete-time walks, the authors derive explicit scaling limits as the dimension tends to infinity, with time averaging taken first, for three random walks. Comparison with continuous-time limits shows agreement only for the simple random walk, so the correspondence between the two models is not universal.

entry.title: Long-time dynamics of the Hubbard model after interaction quenches, using an adaptive ghost Gutzwiller method
entry.summary: Adaptive ghost Gutzwiller dynamics of Hubbard model quenches across coupling strengths over extended times arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper introduces an adaptive time-dependent ghost Gutzwiller approximation that adds auxiliary ghost orbitals whenever correlations grow beyond a threshold, to simulate how correlated electrons evolve in real time. The authors apply it to an interaction quench in the half-filled Hubbard model on a Bethe lattice and compare with numerically exact nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory. Using up to 16 ghost orbitals per spin, the method agrees with the available DMFT data and remains converged for longer times..

entry.title: A classroom experiment on saturated fluorescence spectroscopy using counter-propagating laser beams in atomic vapor
entry.summary: The other side of the saturation coin: an experiment to perform saturation of fluorescence spectroscopy in undergraduate laboratories arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper describes an undergraduate-level experiment in which two counter-propagating laser beams of nearly equal intensity are directed into a room-temperature rubidium-87 vapor cell, and the resulting changes in fluorescence on the D2 transition are measured. It explains the saturation and hyperfine pumping effects using a simple model based on Einstein's population equations, supported by an analysis of relevant timescales. The authors calculate population surfaces to illustrate velocity-selection effects and explain the origin and difference between crossover and atomic resonances.

entry.title: A chip-based gate for trapped ions using only electronic control
entry.summary: All-electronic geometric phase gate on Doppler-cooled trapped ions using an axial mode arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper experimentally demonstrates a high-fidelity entangling gate on two trapped ions using an oscillating magnetic field gradient that drives the axial stretch mode. Only Doppler-cooled ytterbium ions are used, and Bell-state fidelities are reported as far above the relevant fault-tolerant threshold. The control fields consist of an oscillating current in integrated wires and resonant microwave pulses. An adiabatic-elimination version of the gate is also shown to be highly robust.

entry.title: Blueprint for US Energy Department Fault-Tolerant Quantum Supercomputing
entry.summary: Blueprint for DOE Quantum Supercomputing arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper presents a blueprint for preparing the US Department of Energy (DOE) to deploy fault-tolerant quantum computers (FTQCs) for scientific work. It targets initial deployment in 2028 and mature capability in the 2030s. The proposal calls for first-generation systems with at least 100 logical qubits performing 10,000 to 100,000 hard logical operations, along with programming competencies, system software, facility readiness, and focused R&D in applications, algorithms, and logical architectures.

entry.title: Effective long-range interactions in a rectangular lattice under rapid driving, derived semiclassically
entry.summary: Long-range effective interactions in a rectangular tight-binding lattice within the semiclassical approximation arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper extends semiclassical methods of Dunlap–Kenkre and Mamani et al. to a rectangular tight-binding lattice with interactions to all neighbors, under a rapidly oscillating field and an arbitrary static potential. Using a canonical transformation, semiclassical approximation and Kapitza-type time averaging, it derives the effective Hamiltonian. Even-symmetry fields renormalize hopping through Bessel-function factors, while odd-symmetry fields also produce an effective band shift. For the two-dimensional case, the dynamic localization condition is generalized, and the band collapse is shown to be anisotropic.

entry.title: Quantum control when decoherence depends on the control itself
entry.summary: Quantum Control Under Control-Dependent Decoherence arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies how decoherence from a quantum system's coupling to a thermal bath affects coherent quantum control. The authors argue that the dissipative term must depend on the control for the system to relax to a Gibbs state at thermal equilibrium. Using a two-level system coupled to a thermal bath, they compare this control-dependent treatment with a Lindblad-type model where decoherence is time- and control-independent. They find that coherent controls have a greater influence on the dynamics than that model predicts.

entry.title: A quantum solver for flow through porous materials that keeps the fluid incompressible
entry.summary: A Constraint-Preserving Preconditioned Quantum Solver for Heterogeneous Brinkman Flo arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies a quantum method for computing incompressible flow through porous material whose resistance varies in space. The authors rewrite velocity in divergence-free coordinates and introduce a Sobolev–Riesz preconditioner, proving its condition number is bounded by α_max/α_min regardless of grid resolution. They build block encodings and reversible circuits to estimate mean kinetic energy without reconstructing the full velocity field, and identify conditions under which gate complexity beats single-level classical solvers. Numerical tests verify the conditioning bound and circuit accuracy at the tested sizes, but no quantum-hardware runtime advantage is shown.

entry.title: Localization in one-dimensional magnetic quasicrystals
entry.summary: Localization in one-dimensional magnetic quasicrystals arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies localization in a one-dimensional lattice under a quasiperiodic external field, showing that the lattice's graph topology governs the competition between insulating and conducting phases. The authors present models in which all dispersive eigenstates are critically or exponentially localized, coexisting with a flat band of degenerate finitely supported eigenstates. They also construct models with exactly solvable mobility edges arising from graph structure alone. Exact-diagonalization calculations of bosonic dynamics show that on-site interactions drive localized eigenstates toward extendedness, as in the conventional Aubry-André-Harper case.

entry.title: Preparing quantum samples of nonreversible Markov chains using spectral filtering
entry.summary: Quantum State Preparation from Nonreversible Markov Chains via Spectral Filtering arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper presents a framework for preparing and transporting coherent quantum samples of nonreversible Markov chains across a sequence of related chains. It uses spectral filtering to build state-dependent phase operations, combined with fixed-point amplitude amplification. Two constructions are studied: one uses both forward and time-reversed transitions to target the stationary quantum sample, while the other uses only forward transitions and selects the leading eigenstate of a flat discriminant. The paper derives error and resource bounds for the transport procedure.

entry.title: Using Casimir experiments to detect spin-dependent forces
entry.summary: Casimir Experiments as Spin-Force Detectors arXiv · Nov 24, 2026Precision Casimir experiments are sensitive probes of short-range forces but have so far only constrained spin-independent interactions. The paper proposes measuring between reversed polarizations of a magnetically compensated source to directly search for axion-mediated monopole-dipole forces. The spin force changes sign, while common Casimir, gravitational and electrostatic backgrounds broadly cancel. Compensated sources need no intervening shielding, enabling large probes at micrometer gaps.

entry.title: Ground-state chiral quantum clusters: equilibrium many-body states with persistent motion
entry.summary: Ground-State Chiral Quantum Clusters arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper introduces "ground-state chiral quantum clusters," self-bound many-body ground states that carry a persistent current, as an equilibrium analogue of time crystals. The authors give a minimal field theory for these states and an exact microscopic realization using the attractive anyonic Lieb-Liniger model on a ring. In this model, the ground-state density-density correlator shows the Talbot effect, with a soliton-like profile that periodically spreads and revives while drifting indefinitely along the ring. Possible experimental probes are also discussed.

entry.title: Certifying closed labs in device-independent tests of indefinite causal order
entry.summary: Certifying closed labs in device-independent tests of indefinite causality arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper examines how to certify indefinite causal order, where the sequence of events is not fixed, without trusting the devices used. Violations of causal inequalities are meant to rule out definite causal structures, but without the closed laboratories assumption, ordinary two-way communication can produce the same violations. The authors add a minimal set of experimental components that probabilistically probe the process, allowing this assumption to be checked within the protocol.

entry.title: Concentration of the ambiguity function on centered balls
entry.summary: On the concentration of the ambiguity function on centered balls arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper studies how strongly the ambiguity function of a signal concentrates in $L^2$ on every ball centered at the origin. It shows that the Gaussian is the unique function achieving maximal concentration, up to time-frequency shifts and multiplication by a unimodular constant. The proof draws on ideas from quantum information theory.

entry.title: A counterexample to the Ho-Hsieh VQCS saturation conjecture
entry.summary: A counterexample to the Ho-Hsieh VQCS saturation conjecture arXiv · Nov 22, 2026The paper shows that a 4-qubit state can be prepared by a variational quantum-classical simulation (VQCS) circuit with 3 layers but not with 2 layers. This disproves the strong form of Ho and Hsieh's conjecture that VQCS expressivity on L qubits saturates at L/2 layers. The weak form of the conjecture, concerning ground state preparation, remains open.

entry.title: Beyond Quantum Mechanics: Nonlinear, Emergent and Soliton-Based Approaches
entry.summary: Beyond Quantum Mechanics: From Nonlinear to Emergent and Solitonic Approaches arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This thesis examines how nonlinearity could extend or reinterpret quantum mechanics, from modified dynamics to emergent statistical descriptions. It compares Weinberg's nonlinear formulation, de Broglie-Bohm theory, the Madelung formulation and the Hall-Reginatto exact uncertainty approach. It then studies whether quantum dynamics can emerge from the collective statistics of solitons in a fluctuating background, using a Galilean complex sine-Gordon model. Under a weak-noise approximation, the soliton-centre statistics reproduce the Schrödinger equation for Gaussian ensembles and potentials at most quadratic.

entry.title: Energy gap of a confined chiral mode as a measure of critical zero-point fluctuations
entry.summary: Anomalous Hardening of a Fluctuation-Induced Gap arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper studies the excitation gap where uniform and chiral superradiant boundaries meet in a quantum Rabi ring. The gap is proportional to the uniform zero-point variance divided by the frequency ratio η, closing as η^-2/3 while the variance grows as η^1/3. A quartic Schrödinger equation matches full spin-photon diagonalization, and a triangle of spins with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya exchange follows the same relation with a different coefficient.

entry.title: A paper showing two messages suffice for quantum interactive proof systems
entry.summary: Two messages suffice for quantum interactive proof systems arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies how many message rounds quantum interactive proof systems need. The authors show that any quantum interactive proof system can be parallelized to two messages, where the verifier sends halves of EPR pairs as quantum public coins and then uses only stoquastic verification after the prover responds. This fully characterizes two-message quantum interactive proof systems, which are shown to equal PSPACE. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that any quantum interactive proof compresses to two messages and, via PSPACE-hardness of CIUniform, fully characterize two-message systems.

entry.title: Quantum Subentropy: Subadditivity and Sharp Bounds on Discrimination Error
entry.summary: Quantum Subentropy: Subadditivity and Sharp Bounds on Discrimination Error arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies quantum subentropy, which gives a tight spectral lower bound on the accessible information of pure-state ensembles. The authors prove subadditivity for arbitrary finite-dimensional bipartite states and derive a sharp relation between conditional subentropy and the minimum discrimination error. They also determine the optimal Lipschitz constant in trace distance for conditional subentropy on classical-quantum states, and show that strong subadditivity fails for quantum states while holding for classical distributions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove subadditivity of subentropy for finite-dimensional bipartite states and a sharp relation between conditional subentropy and minimum discrimination error. They report a counterexample

entry.title: A paper advancing the theory of approximate quantum measurements and recovery operations
entry.summary: Advancing the Theory of Pretty Good Quantum Operations arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper addresses the difficulty of finding optimal quantum measurements or recovery maps.
