It unifies pretty good measurements and Petz maps within a semidefinite programming framework with a tunable power, extending them to broader quantum tasks. For powers between one and three, it proves a stronger performance bound than the Barnum-Knill bound, which peaks at quadratic power. For structured channels such as stabilizer codes under Pauli noise, large powers make recovery approach a maximum likelihood decoder for maximally mixed inputs. ★★★★ Notable: The authors unify pretty good measurements and Petz maps in a tunable-power SDP framework and report a stronger bound than Barnum-Knill for powers from one to three.

entry.title: Cutting RSA-2048 factoring Toffoli counts below one billion using LLM-driven verifiable quantum compilation
entry.summary: Reducing RSA-2048 Factoring Resources Below One Billion Toffolis via LLM-Driven Verifiable Quantum Compilation arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies quantum circuits that use Shor's algorithm to factor 2048-bit RSA integers, redesigning an approximate residue number system pipeline with large language model-driven search. The authors build a deterministic compiler that produces a Pareto frontier of RSA-2048 circuits and analytically bound rare overflow probabilities. They verify elementary gate sequences across the RNS primes on representative circuits. Against Gidney's 2025 baseline under matched adder accounting, the paper reports a 70.1% reduction in minimum qubit-Toffoli product and up to 78.6% fewer expected factoring Toffolis, bringing RSA-2048 factoring below one billion Toffolis. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use LLM-driven search to redesign an RNS pipeline, reporting RSA-2048 factoring below one billion Toffolis versus Gidney's 2025 baseline.

entry.title: Linear entanglement suffices for f-routing: a quantum communication result
entry.summary: Linear entanglement suffices for f-routing arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies f-routing, a task in which Alice and Bob share a pre-prepared quantum state and each send one simultaneous message, after which the party chosen by a Boolean function f(x,y) recovers an unknown qubit. The authors show that 2n+2 shared EPR pairs suffice for every function f, improving the previous best bound for all functions, which was 2^{O(√(n log n))} qubits. The new strategy shifts the cost from the shared state to the messages, with Alice sending 2^{n+1}+1 qubits and Bob sending only classical bits. The result is formalized in Lean. ★★★★ Notable: The authors reduce the all-function entanglement upper bound from 2^O(√(n log n)) to 2n+2 EPR pairs, with the result formalized in Lean.

entry.title: Exponential gains in probing quantum systems by adding a single extra qubit
entry.summary: Exponential advantage in quantum observation with one extra qubit arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper proposes an algorithm that adds one extra qubit to a quantum machine to probe quantum many-body dynamics. The qubit coherently interferes dynamical trajectories, allowing exponentially many multi-time correlators to be estimated with exponentially fewer evolutions than ancilla-free schemes. Numerical experiments on a many-body system show higher-order probe signals predicted with orders-of-magnitude fewer experimental runs than previous methods. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose using one extra qubit to interfere trajectories, exponentially reducing runs, and report a proof of optimality plus numerical demonstration.

entry.title: Measuring superposition using quantum coherence via stochastic orthogonalization
entry.summary: Quantifying superposition via coherence by stochastic orthogonalization arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper proposes a way to measure how much a state is a superposition of nonorthogonal reference states, using quantum coherence. The authors show that orthogonalization can be realized as a measurement that maps each reference state onto a basis vector multiple, and define a state's degree of superposition from the largest average coherence such measurements extract. The paper also examines when one superposition can be converted into another with certainty. ★★★★ Notable: The authors define superposition degree via stochastic orthogonalization, turning any coherence measure into a superposition measure, and report a tight bound for interference terms.

entry.title: Universal stabilizer correlations in chaotic eigenstates
entry.summary: Universal stabilizer correlations in chaotic eigenstates arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies the stabilizer correlation, defined as the difference between the Rényi-2 mutual information and the mutual stabilizer Rényi entropy, which captures structure in quantum states beyond entanglement and nonstabilizerness. For chaotic eigenstates, the authors show that this correlation approaches a universal constant determined only by symmetries. The value is derived analytically from random-state ensembles for different symmetry classes and confirmed by exact calculations on a chaotic mixed-field Ising chain. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a universal stabilizer correlation constant for chaotic eigenstates, derived analytically from random-state ensembles and checked on a mixed-field Ising chain.

entry.title: Joint measurements and state updates in quantum field theory, tested with a Bell inequality
entry.summary: For whom the Bell tolls: joint measurements and state updates in quantum field theory arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper studies state update rules in the Fewster-Verch measurement framework for quantum field theory and their behaviour in Bell tests. For observables of the form A(f_i)*A(f_i), it derives the joint moment generating functional and a unique joint probability distribution. As an application, it builds a Bell test model using a coupled Proca-scalar model for polarization measurements and shows that this model can violate the CHSH inequality. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive joint moment generating functionals for commuting observables in the Fewster-Verch framework and build a QFT Bell test model reported to violate CHSH.

entry.title: Effect of structured noise on bosonic quantum error correction: how environmental noise can reshape photon-loss errors.
entry.summary: Impact of structured noise on bosonic quantum error correction arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper reports experiments in a three-dimensional circuit quantum electrodynamics system, injecting spectrally engineered environmental noise into a weakly nonlinear oscillator. The measured Fock-state dynamics show clear frequency selectivity, with long-time transition rates converging to the Markovian limit while transient dynamics are non-Markovian, in quantitative agreement with a second-order time-convolutionless theory. Applying narrowband noise to a binomially encoded logical qubit, the authors demonstrate Fock-state-dependent dissipation channels that drive logical states beyond the nominally correctable error space. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report Fock-state-dependent photon loss from structured noise, matching a second-order TCL theory and driving binomially encoded logical states beyond the correctable error space.

entry.title: Expressivity of Observables in Fixed-Readout Quantum Neural Networks
entry.summary: Observable-Level Expressivity in Fixed-Readout Quantum Neural Networks arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies which effective observables a quantum neural network with a fixed readout can realize, comparing three physical resource classes: unitary, mixed-unitary, and completely positive trace-preserving (CPTP) evolution. The authors show the reachable sets are strictly nested. They give an amplitude-damping example lying outside the mixed-unitary level and derive closed-form loss floors for each level. ★★★★ Notable: The authors characterize reachable effective observables by physical resource class, giving strict inclusions and closed-form loss floors reproduced numerically, plus structured and classification exp

entry.title: Experiment distributing entanglement between atoms at 500 Hz over city-scale fiber
entry.summary: 500 Hz atom-atom entanglement distribution over metropolitan-scale fibers arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper reports an experiment that distributes entanglement between remote atoms over 20 km of optical fiber using two 15 by 15 quantum memory arrays. It generates matter-matter entanglement at 546 Hz without active phase stabilization. The authors state this rate exceeds two-photon and single-photon schemes by factors of 75,932 and 23, and argue the method combines efficiency and robustness for multiplexed quantum repeaters. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report 546 Hz remote atom-atom entanglement over 20 km fiber using two 15×15 quantum memory arrays, unifying efficiency and robustness.

entry.title: Energy limit when replicating fragments in PQG reduced-density-matrix theory
entry.summary: The replication-energy limit of PQG reduced-density-matrix theory from a single-fragment semidefinite program arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper studies a size-extensivity problem in variational two-electron reduced-density-matrix calculations, where the energy per fragment can decrease when identical noninteracting fragments are replicated. For the PQG conditions, the authors show that the energy per fragment converges to the minimum of a semidefinite program on a single fragment. The analysis also covers monotonicity in replica count and the role of local electron-number variance, with examples including Be, CH4, N2, H2O and a four-site Hubbard fragment. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove the PQG per-fragment energy limit equals a single-fragment SDP minimum, reached at finite replica count; examples include molecules and a Hubbard fragment.

entry.title: What quantum networks can guarantee about the entangled pairs they deliver
entry.summary: What can a quantum network promise about the entangled pairs it delivers? arXiv · Nov 23, 2026Quantum networks deliver entangled qubit pairs, but users cannot measure each pair's fidelity without destroying it, so networks usually promise quality based on a physical model. The paper shows that secretly testing some pairs at random lets users bound the average fidelity of the pairs they keep without relying on a model. Testing only a small fraction, however, cannot reliably guarantee that every kept pair meets a threshold. The authors give a rule that limits the risk of receiving a bad pair, provided the model is not overly optimistic or a sufficient margin is declared in advance. ★★★★ Notable: The authors separate average from per-pair fidelity guarantees, giving a model-free average lower bound and a model-conditional per-pair risk bound; the abstract reports validation on a 36-qubit trapp

entry.title: Local redundancies are necessary for long-lived memories in finite spatial dimensions
entry.summary: Local redundancies are necessary for long-lived memories in finite spatial dimensions arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper proves a no-go theorem against exponentially long-lived thermal memories, based on redundancies among Hamiltonian terms. For local stabilizer Hamiltonians without local redundancies, it shows that at any constant nonzero temperature, local heat-bath dynamics mixes fast, with O(N) mixing time, where N is the number of qubits. Under a stronger condition on induced redundancies, it proves rapid mixing with O(log N) mixing time. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that without local redundancies, heat-bath dynamics mixes fast, with O(log N) mixing time shown under stronger redundancy conditions, including Haah's cubic code.

entry.title: Tighter upper limits on two-way capacity for amplitude-damping quantum channels
entry.summary: Improved two-way capacity upper bounds for amplitude-damping channels arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper gives an improved upper bound, log₂[1+(1-γ)γ^{γ/(1-γ)}], on the two-way-assisted capacities of the qubit amplitude-damping channel with decay probability γ. The bound applies to quantum communication, entanglement distribution, private communication and secret-key agreement. The authors extend sector teleportation simulation to qubits and determine the exact additive relative entropy of entanglement of amplitude-damping resources. They also derive explicit bounds for generalized amplitude damping, which includes thermal excitation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive an improved two-way capacity upper bound for amplitude-damping channels, extending sector teleportation simulation to qubits and reporting strict gains over known bounds.

entry.title: How phase rigidity scales with system size without eigenstate merging
entry.summary: Scaling of phase rigidity without eigenstate coalescence arXiv · Nov 22, 2026The paper studies how non-Hermitian skin effects determine the way phase rigidity changes with system size, without any eigenstate coalescence. Exact analytical results are derived for three non-Hermitian chain models and checked numerically. Phase rigidity decays exponentially under the ordinary skin effect, approaches a nonzero constant as N^-2 under the scale-free skin effect, and can decay as N^-1/2 to zero under the algebraic skin effect. These results show that eigenstate nonorthogonality can be controlled without exceptional points. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show skin effects give distinct phase-rigidity scaling without eigenstate coalescence, reporting exact results for three chain models with numerical checks.

entry.title: Generalized second law derived from fluctuation theorems in a quantum reference frame
entry.summary: The Generalized Second Law from Fluctuation Theorems in a Quantum Reference Frame arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper proves the generalized second law (GSL) for black-hole exteriors undergoing unitary driving and relaxation on a fixed semifinite algebra. Instead of Wall's approach, which assumes semiclassical geometry and restricts to algebras of successive horizon cuts, it evolves the state on a fixed dressed exterior algebra and uses a gravitational charge as a quantum clock. The authors formulate the GSL through a quantum channel fluctuation theorem, giving three complementary versions. They establish entropy bounds that yield the GSL in a slow-clock limit and quantify finite-width clock corrections. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use a gravitational charge as a quantum clock to build a modular crossed product and derive the GSL via a channel fluctuation theorem, with bounds in a slow-clock limit.

entry.title: Undecidable quantum storage: whether a fixed circuit keeps quantum information cannot be determined from noise rate alone
entry.summary: Undecidable quantum storage: no algorithm can tell from the noise rate whether a fixed circuit remembers arXiv · Nov 22, 2026The paper constructs fixed local quantum circuits for which no algorithm can determine, from the noise rate alone, whether the circuit can store a qubit for a long time under one-dimensional single-qubit noise. Disjoint rate intervals are indexed by inputs to a universal Turing machine: if the machine runs forever, a qubit is stored for a time growing with system size, while if it halts, fidelity drops below a fixed bound. These are existence results with very large system sizes and very small noise rates. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors build fixed local circuits from a universal Turing machine so that noise rate alone cannot decide storage, with encoding and decoding maps giving storage and failure results.

entry.title: Total information from pairs of alternative quantum measurements, bounded by Holevo information
entry.summary: Holevo-Bounded Total Information from Pair Distributions of Alternative Quantum Measurements arXiv · Nov 21, 2026The paper studies quantum ensembles whose accessible information can be strictly smaller than their Holevo information, and asks whether information spread across two alternative measurement contexts can close this gap without assigning a joint distribution to their outcomes. Building on a relative-entropy projection method by Harder et al., it defines a directed posterior novelty for each record and an associated total-information quantity. For finite-dimensional classical-quantum ensembles, it proves that optimizing this quantity over pairs of POVMs yields a value between the accessible and Holevo information. ★★★★ Notable: The authors define a pair-measurement total-information quantity bounded between accessible and Holevo information, saturating Holevo on BB84, and settle quantum validity of an information causality c

entry.title: How quantum resources limit function approximation
entry.summary: Quantum resources constrain function approximation arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies how four quantum resources (coherence, imaginarity, entanglement, and magic) constrain what a quantum learning model can approximate, with a fixed encoding and readout. In a one-qubit phase-encoding model, coherence bounds the oscillation of the model function and imaginarity bounds its odd part. For domains away from zero, Clifford trainable gates suffice for uniform approximation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors link coherence, imaginarity, entanglement and magic to function-approximation bounds, and report a polynomial Clifford-replacement result for magic.

entry.title: Quantum algorithms for simulating low-temperature impurity models at high precision
entry.summary: Quantum simulation of low-temperature impurity models arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies quantum impurity models, in which a small, strongly interacting subsystem couples to a large non-interacting bath, a core computational tool in dynamical mean field theory. The authors develop quantum algorithms that simulate these models at low temperatures with high precision, using global jump operators to avoid the exponential overhead common in quantum Gibbs samplers. They give polynomial-time algorithms for preparing thermal states, their purifications, and ground states, and estimate static and dynamical properties with Heisenberg scaling. ★★★★ Notable: Global jump operators avoid the exp(beta) overhead of quantum Gibbs samplers, giving polynomial-time low-temperature thermal-state preparation for impurity models with Heisenberg scaling.

entry.title: Simple adaptive protocol design for quantum metrology with limited data
entry.summary: Simple design of adaptive protocols for quantum metrology with limited data arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper proposes a simple Bayesian design principle for adaptive protocols in quantum metrology, based on Personick's minimum mean square loss formalism. It jointly optimises the measurement and the probe, extending earlier methods that only adjusted control parameters. In adaptive phase estimation with single-mode Gaussian probes, the joint optimisation outperforms adaptive homodyne detection and a fixed probe optimised for the initial prior, reducing mean posterior variance by up to 32% relative to homodyne detection.

entry.title: Small-world networks produce tunable quantum error-correcting codes at shallow circuit depth
entry.summary: Small-world networks yield tunable quantum codes at short circuit depth arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper generates quantum error-correcting codes by running random Clifford circuits on Watts–Strogatz small-world networks. Three parameters, nonlocal graph rewiring, measurement rate, and circuit depth, are used to tune code properties. On fully rewired networks, logarithmic-depth circuits yield codes with finite rate and lower failure probability than local circuits, forming at depth growing as ln n. Rewiring also shifts the purification transition to higher measurement rates and changes its critical exponents.

entry.title: Estimating stabilizer fidelity using single-copy Pauli measurements
entry.summary: Self-guided estimation of the stabilizer fidelity with single-copy Pauli measurements arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper addresses the difficulty of estimating stabilizer fidelity, a measure of how non-stabilizer a quantum state is. It proposes a self-guided protocol for unknown pure or mixed states that needs only single-copy Pauli measurements. The method moves through neighboring stabilizer states, reuses earlier results, and certifies the global optimum when the fidelity's lower confidence bound exceeds cos²(π/8). Numerical simulations on up to 14 qubits reached the optimum in every run, with few iterations that grow only slightly with qubit number.

entry.title: Floquet spectra and entanglement sensitivity in the quantum kicked top
entry.summary: Floquet spectra and parameter sensitivity of entanglement in the quantum kicked top arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies how the Floquet spectrum of the quantum kicked top relates to how sensitive its entanglement pattern is to changes in parameters and starting conditions. Using four qubits, the authors locate degeneracies in the Floquet eigenphases with a resultant of the characteristic polynomial and its derivative, and map entanglement sensitivity to kick strength across spin coherent initial states. They find that sensitivity maxima coincide with eigenphase degeneracies or with kick strengths showing short-period quantum revivals.

entry.title: A readout method for charge detection that uses nonlinear resonators to protect the sensor
entry.summary: Protected Charge Readout Scheme Utilizing Nonlinear Resonators arXiv · Nov 24, 2026Charge detection in nanoscale quantum devices often uses dissipative sensors, where absorbed signal causes measurement backaction. The paper shows that the frequency shift induced in nonlinear resonators, which previously gave near-unity readout signals, also detunes the resonator from the measurement signal and thereby protects the sensor. Numerical modeling indicates that resonator excitation is reduced while the enhanced readout signal is maintained, combining strong readout contrast with less measurement-induced backaction.

entry.title: A quantum model built from the Riemann-Siegel formula, for locating zeta-function zeros
entry.summary: A Quantum Model from the Riemann-Siegel Formula arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper builds a two-component quantum model in which destructive interference selects zeros of a regularized zeta function lying on the critical line. It starts from the Riemann-Siegel integral representation, subtracts the pole contribution at the origin, and applies a Dirichlet heat filter and an arithmetic dressing based on prime-power dilations. The computed lower critical-line zeros lie close to known Riemann zeros, with spacing and pair-correlation statistics consistent with the Gaussian unitary ensemble over the sampled range. Whether all analytic zeros in the lower half of the critical strip belong to the physical spectral family remains open.

entry.title: How well entangling gates resist correlated noise in qubits
entry.summary: Resilience of Entangling Gates to Spatiotemporally Correlated Noise arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies how spatially and temporally correlated noise limits the fidelity of two-qubit entangling gates. For semiconductor spin qubits, the CZ and √iSWAP gates are shown to be more resilient to correlated noise than the SWAP gate. The authors derive a general expression for average gate infidelity under arbitrary spatiotemporal noise correlations, written as a spectral overlap between the noise correlation matrix and a gate-dependent filter function. The framework turns measured noise correlations into error budgets and offers a design principle for choosing entangling operations.

entry.title: Solving the traveling salesman problem on quantum devices using QUBO and HOBO models
entry.summary: Solving the Traveling Salesman Problem Using Quantum Devices: QUBO and HOBO Formulations arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper examines how quantum devices can solve the traveling salesman problem, a classic hard optimization task used in logistics. It compares two ways of encoding the problem: the QUBO formulation, which needs many qubits, and the HOBO formulation, which needs fewer qubits but includes higher-order terms. The authors provide a practical approach for solving the problem and compare the two formulations in detail.

entry.title: Wigner negativity costs phase-space area: a conjectured sharpening of the Lieb–Solovej inequality
entry.summary: Wigner negativity costs phase-space area: A conjectured refinement of the Lieb--Solovej inequality at Rényi order one half arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper conjectures that the Wigner logarithmic negativity of a single-mode quantum state is bounded by how much the Rényi-1/2 entropy of its Husimi function exceeds the coherent-state value, with equality only for coherent states. If true, this refines the Lieb–Solovej inequality with a resource-monotone remainder term. The authors prove the conjecture for all states up to an additive constant ln 2, and show the conjecture fails for the Wehrl entropy and higher Rényi orders.

entry.title: Drift-resistant control pulses that reduce recalibration of silicon spin qubits
entry.summary: Mitigating drift in spin-qubit control with calibration-insensitive pulses arXiv · Nov 24, 2026Silicon spin qubits need their control parameters retuned every few hours because device calibration drifts. This study replaces square pulses with the adiabatic BIR-4 and composite CORPSE pulses and tests them on a Si/SiGe quantum-dot device. BIR-4 keeps about 99% Clifford fidelity across a factor-of-2 change in drive power, and it holds its rotation angle to 0.3 degrees over ten days without recalibration.

entry.title: Programmable broadband polarization-preserving optical delay line using Faraday mirrors
entry.summary: Programmable Broadband Polarization-Preserving Optical Delay Line with Faraday Mirrors arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper presents a broadband optical delay line that is programmable for delays up to 1 microsecond with nanosecond resolution while preserving an arbitrary, unknown input polarization state. It uses cascaded standard single-mode fiber segments, with an optical switch selecting a short or long path in each segment, and Faraday mirrors at both ends that automatically compensate random polarization fluctuations from the fibers. Numerical experiments show a mean output polarization fidelity better than 99% over a 50-nm range around the central wavelength.

entry.title: Noise-resistant attractor states in randomly driven non-Hermitian systems
entry.summary: Noise-Immune Attractors in Stochastically Driven Non-Hermitian Systems arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies non-Hermitian quantum systems subject to random time-dependent fluctuations. The authors derive an exact noise master equation for Gaussian fluctuations and identify a noise-invariance mechanism driven by T-symmetry-broken Liouvillian attractors. This mechanism yields stable defect-density plateaus and an exact classification into noise-independent, fully polarized, and continuously tunable regimes. The results are examined in an imbalanced-pairing non-Hermitian Kitaev model.

entry.title: Multipartite entanglement in crystal quenches: how tripartite entanglement arises and spreads after a quantum quench
entry.summary: Multipartite entanglement structure of crystal quenches arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies how multipartite entanglement emerges and spreads after a quantum quench, focusing on quasiparticle multiplets generated by crystal quenches in a tight-binding chain. The authors identify zero-configurations in which a tripartite-shared multiplet contains no irreducible tripartite entanglement and consists only of pairwise bipartite entangled states. They build a quasiparticle picture for the Markov gap and show it is a faithful witness of irreducible tripartite entanglement in crystal quenches. The results are compared with exact lattice numerics and agree perfectly in the hydrodynamic regime.

entry.title: Electron transport through two interacting quantum dots showing interference oscillations
entry.summary: Aharonov-Bohm oscillations in transport through interacting quantum dots arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper studies electron transport through a two-terminal Aharonov-Bohm interferometer containing two quantum dots with finite intra-dot Coulomb interactions. Using a diagrammatic technique and linear perturbation theory, the authors derive analytic expressions for occupations, current, and interferometric visibility, with some symmetric setups giving closed-form conductance. The analysis shows that a finite Coulomb interaction strongly affects visibility, with destructive interference rapidly suppressed when system symmetries are broken.

entry.title: A quantum engine that runs on dephasing noise, with time-crystal work cycles
entry.summary: Dephasing-Powered Autonomous Quantum Engine with Time-Crystalline Work Cycles arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper proposes an autonomous quantum engine that uses local dephasing, usually treated as harmful noise, as its energy source. Dephasing disrupts ferromagnetic correlations in an interacting spin ensemble, and the injected energy is transferred through an LC resonator to a passive load. Without external periodic driving, the system self-organizes into a time-crystalline work cycle that delivers sustained, reproducible power.

entry.title: Efficient Shot Allocation and Spectral Reconstruction for Real-Time Quantum Krylov Diagonalization
entry.summary: Efficient Shot Allocation and Spectral Reconstruction for Real-Time Quantum Krylov Diagonalization arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper presents analytical and statistical methods for improving energy estimates from real-time quantum Krylov diagonalization when the number of measurements is fixed. It derives the leading energy variance as a function of shots per circuit setting and uses an initial batch of measurements to allocate the remaining shots. The resulting generalized least-squares estimator minimizes the leading mean-square error within the allocation class. Numerical experiments on spin and Hubbard models show that learned allocation and enforcing spectral consistency reduce energy estimation error.

entry.title: Geometric properties of chained geometric and holonomic quantum gates
entry.summary: Geometric properties of concatenated geometric and holonomic quantum gates arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies how geometric and holonomic quantum computation behave when quantum gates are concatenated. It shows that a sequence of individually geometric gates is not generally geometric, because the composite operation can accumulate nontrivial dynamical phases. It further shows that concatenations of arbitrary single-qubit holonomic gates remain holonomic when the parallel-transport condition holds and the computational subspace evolves cyclically.

entry.title: Transferring quantum coherence between two parties with misaligned bases over a capacity-limited channel
entry.summary: Coherence transfer under bounded channel capacity arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies how quantum coherence can be transferred between two parties whose local reference bases do not match, when the quantum channel has limited capacity. Within the resource theory of coherence, Alice is restricted to maximally incoherent operations in her basis, and the goal is to maximize the coherence Bob receives. The authors analyze two single-shot protocols, direct transmission and transmission via local entanglement, and derive their phase-optimized coherence yields, including averaged performance when Bob's basis is unknown. For single-qubit transmission, they give an analytical lower bound and identify a regime where the optimal yield reaches the channel capacity.

entry.title: Controlling dark modes in a three-mode optomechanical system using Floquet sidebands
entry.summary: Floquet dark-mode manipulation in a three-mode optomechanical system arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper proposes a Floquet sideband method to control the dark-mode effect in a system where one cavity mode couples to two mechanical modes. Periodic frequency modulation of one mechanical mode generates sidebands, and one sideband is tuned to match the other mechanical mode, producing a mechanical dark mode decoupled from the cavity. The authors check the approximate Hamiltonian's validity through state fidelity and demonstrate control by tracking bright and dark mode populations after a sudden frequency detuning. The results may support future work on quantum-state storage using Floquet mechanical dark modes.

entry.title: Reproducing kernel and matrix representation of the deformed quantum optical density operator of R(p,q) super-coherent states
entry.summary: Reproducing kernel and matrix representation of the deformed quantum optical density operator of R(p,q)-super-coherent states on B₀oplusB₁ fermionic quantum algebra arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies R(p,q) super-coherent states with two Grassmann variables, built on the superalgebra B0⊕B1 from R(p,q)-deformed quantum algebras. The super-Fock space splits into bosonic, two fermionic, and bi-fermionic sectors, each with a diagonal representation of the density operator, and the total density operator is the sum of the four sectoral contributions. The authors define sectorial reproducing kernels and prove their hermiticity, positivity and matrix multiplication properties. In the bosonic sector, Berezin quantization and the dispersions of super-position and super-momentum operators show that these states are intelligent states.

entry.title: Imaging how magnetization flips and domains move in a nonlinear, energy-losing way using quantum sensors
entry.summary: Quantum Imaging of Nonlinear Magnetization Reversal and Dissipative Domain Dynamics arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper presents a stroboscopic quantum diamond microscope that uses nitrogen-vacancy centres to probe the AC response of a Pt/Co/Pt thin film. The method overcomes the limited dynamic range of conventional optically detected magnetic resonance imaging and observes magnetization reversal under large-amplitude sinusoidal and square wave fields. Phase delays reveal energy dissipation, and higher-order harmonics give access to the nonlinear AC susceptibility.

entry.title: Binary-tree quantum algorithm for splitting a graph into k parts to maximize cut edges
entry.summary: Binary-Tree Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm for the Maximum k-Cut Problem arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper proposes a binary-tree quantum approximate optimization algorithm (BT-QAOA) for the maximum k-cut problem. Instead of encoding all k subset assignments per vertex, it applies standard MaxCut QAOA to at most 2k-3 subproblems, splitting only the subset with the largest cut-value gain at each step. The authors derive a theoretical lower bound on the approximation ratio and report simulations showing reduced qubit and gate overhead while keeping a high approximation ratio.

entry.title: Liouvillian Quasiparticle Spectroscopy: Probing Quasiparticles in Open Quantum Many-Body Systems
entry.summary: Liouvillian Quasiparticle Spectroscopy arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper extends the quasiparticle concept to open quantum systems, defining coherent quasiparticles by responses to perturbations on one side of the density matrix and incoherent ones by perturbations on both sides. It proposes spectroscopy protocols that couple the system to auxiliary levels to measure their complex energies. Numerical simulations of models with skin effects show that the two types can propagate in opposite directions, and reveal gapless Nambu-Goldstone modes in the weak and strong-to-weak U(1) symmetry-breaking models.

entry.title: Exact limits on finite-sample and loss-constrained phase estimation with squeezed vacuum
entry.summary: Exact finite-sample and loss limits of squeezed-vacuum phase estimation arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper uses exact computation to determine finite-sample errors, resource-fair scaling, phase windows, and loss ceilings for squeezed-vacuum phase estimation. It finds that a fixed overhead of ten repetitions sets the attainable finite-sample frontier, but these repetitions cancel in the resource-fair bound, so Heisenberg scaling still holds. It also reports that fixed loss caps the per-photon advantage at a value determined only by transmissivity, a value the reported record already reaches.

entry.title: Confidence-aware classifier readout for fast neutral-atom qubit detection
entry.summary: Confidence-Aware Discriminative Readout of Neutral-Atom Arrays arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper demonstrates a readout method for neutral-atom arrays of 171Yb atoms in optical tweezers that outputs a measurement reliability score instead of a hard binary result. A logistic-regression classifier uses total photon counts and the spatial fluorescence pattern at each site. At 10 ms exposure it reaches 99.83% readout fidelity, comparable to 99.82% from conventional thresholding at 20 ms. The scores allow low-confidence outcomes to be converted into erasures and reduce false positives, and Monte Carlo rearrangement simulations suggest improved defect-free assembly.

entry.title: Thermodynamics and superfluid transition of a 2D Bose gas across interaction strengths
entry.summary: Universal thermodynamics and BKT transition of the planar Bose gas from weak to strong interactions arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper uses the functional renormalization group to compute universal thermodynamics of a dilute two-dimensional Bose gas at weak and strong coupling. The equation of state is nearly insensitive to the approximation scheme, differing by only a few percent even at strong coupling. The improved approximation also reproduces the universal superfluid density jump and critical anomalous dimension at the BKT transition to within a few percent.

entry.title: Critical Topology: A Review of Topological Phase Transitions
entry.summary: Critical Topology: A New Perspective for Phase Transitions arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This review paper discusses critical topology, a form of quantum criticality beyond the Landau paradigm that adds topological properties to the classification of universality classes. It outlines open questions, including a general criterion for its emergence, unified frameworks beyond one dimension, and numerical methods for higher-dimensional strongly correlated systems. The authors also note that experiments so far focus on single-particle cases and that realizing many-body critical topology on platforms such as Rydberg atom arrays is a key next step.

entry.title: Privacy-enhanced distributed sensing network using causal-order switching and probe squeezing
entry.summary: Privacy-Enhanced Distributed Sensing Network via Causal-Order Switching and Probe Squeezing arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper addresses information leakage risks when multiple users share sensitive sensor data, quantifying network privacy with the maximum information leakage ratio (MILR). It proposes a protocol combining causal-order switching, which encodes privacy using network propagation dynamics, and probe squeezing, which suppresses leakage through quantum channels. The mechanism is demonstrated experimentally in distributed beam-tilt sensing with spatially structured light, without nonclassical light sources.

entry.title: Combining state and operator evolution to extend quantum many-body simulations
entry.summary: Combining Schrödinger and Heisenberg Evolution to Extend Quantum Many-Body Simulations arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper combines separate evolution of quantum states (Schrödinger picture) and observables (Heisenberg picture), joining them through massively parallel tensor-network contractions to reach longer evolution times than either method alone. The authors implement this with tree tensor networks and sparse Pauli propagation. They simulate the magnetization of an 11×11 open lattice in a quench of the two-dimensional transverse-field Ising model at the critical field, comparing results with iPEPS, numerical linked-cluster expansion, and X-truncated sparse Pauli dynamics.

entry.title: Remotely charging quantum batteries through a multimode resonator
entry.summary: Remote Charging of Quantum Batteries via a Multimode Resonator arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies how a qubit charger coupled through a finite multimode resonator can remotely charge a qubit battery. It uses time-shifted coupling pulses that account for the spatial phases of the resonator modes, and compares stored energy with ergotropy, the maximum work extractable by a local unitary operation. Without loss, stronger coupling lets the battery reach positive ergotropy sooner, while the final charge stays nearly complete. After disconnection, stored energy decays exponentially, but ergotropy vanishes at a finite time.

entry.title: Which entangled subspaces can hold PPT states, and how complementary pairs behave
entry.summary: Positive-partial-transpose structure of completely entangled subspaces and their complements arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies completely entangled subspaces (CESs), which contain no product vectors, and asks whether they can support states with positive partial transpose (PPT). The authors use a semidefinite criterion that minimizes the smallest partial-transpose eigenvalue over all supported density operators. For two-qutrit states, they fully characterize when a CES supports PPT states: exactly when it is four-dimensional and locally equivalent to the complement of an unextendible product basis. The paper also gives explicit constructions of complementary CES pairs in 3⊗4 and 4⊗4.

entry.title: Spectral analysis of a hidden near-horizon reflection at the boundary
entry.summary: Boundary spectroscopy of hidden near-horizon reflection arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper studies the boundary response of a scalar field in a rotating Bañados-Teitelboim-Zanelli exterior. It derives an exact response for a corotating passive wall near the horizon and gives its spectrum using an Airy filter. On any frequency band, the response identifies the wall's constant impedance and position, whereas a perfect absorber is exponentially hidden.

entry.title: Reconstructing pure-state OTOCs from forward-time linear response
entry.summary: Reconstructing Pure-State OTOCs from Forward-Time Linear Response arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper shows that the connected out-of-time-ordered correlator (OTOC) of any pure state can be exactly reconstructed from commutator linear responses alone. The protocol needs no time reversal, ancilla, double copy, or weak measurement, only a unitary string pulse, forward evolution, and a single local readout. Restricting pulses to a fixed operator weight makes the measurement sparse and turns truncation into an analytically controlled spectral filter. Exact-diagonalization benchmarks in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model and a nonintegrable Ising chain confirm the predictions.

entry.title: Geometric polarization-virial theorems for field-induced dipole forces and their reversal
entry.summary: Geometric Polarization-Virial Theorems for Field-Induced Dipolar Interactions and Force Reversal arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies how an electric field can turn the attraction between far-apart atoms into repulsion. The authors identify a geometric structure in which the cubically weighted interaction free energy, r^3 F(r), does not decrease under physical dilation. From this they derive two exact polarization-virial theorems for stable quasistatic dipole assemblies and fully retarded dipole pairs. A coupled quantum harmonic oscillator pair is used to obtain the interaction energy and radial force at arbitrary angles, separating the energy-zero and force-zero angles.

entry.title: Quantum amplitude estimation for finding ligand and pose indices
entry.summary: Quantum Amplitude Estimation for Ligand and Pose Index Retrieval arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper proposes a quantum virtual screening framework that aims to directly retrieve ligand and pose indices meeting a threshold, without computing a full interaction-score table. It uses quantum amplitude estimation built on quantum phase estimation, with optional Grover-style quantum selection to amplify selected outcomes. The approach is evaluated on an ideal logical benchmark using AutoDock grid interactions as a proof-of-concept model.

entry.title: Spin-adapted state preparation for efficient quantum chemistry simulation
entry.summary: Spin-adapted state preparation for quantum chemistry arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper addresses preparing initial states with high overlap to the ground state for quantum phase estimation on strongly correlated molecules. It shows that spin-adapted matrix product states can be treated as abelian-symmetric block-sparse MPS and loaded with existing protocols, followed by one state-independent rotation per site. Resource estimates for singlet ground states of iron-sulphur cluster active space models report Toffoli count reductions of up to 135 times versus dense methods and 4.9 times versus block-sparse methods, with up to 3.7 times fewer ancilla qubits.

entry.title: Coherences between electronic states in molecules driven by several photons at once.
entry.summary: Multiphoton Electronic Coherences in Molecules arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper studies multiphoton electronic coherences in gas-phase atoms and molecules of increasing complexity. It uses pairs of phase-locked deep-ultraviolet pulses with independently controlled relative phase and time delay. By combining ionization yields measured at specific relative phases, the authors isolate different photon orders and measure coherences between specific electronic state pairs. Fast electronic dynamics are tracked alongside nuclear motion, and analytic expressions for the ionization yield versus pump-probe delay are derived.

entry.title: Cqlib: A high-performance software toolkit for quantum computing
entry.summary: Cqlib: A High-Performance Software Stack for Quantum Computing arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper presents Cqlib, a software stack for quantum computing built on a unified quantum circuit model, with a Rust core and Python and C interfaces. It covers program construction, simulation, compilation, and result processing, and supports execution on QCIS-compatible quantum hardware via OpenQASM and QCIS. The stack also includes a modular algorithm library and application-level modules for chemistry, optimization, and machine learning.

entry.title: A proposed scheme to rapidly generate entangled cat-state chains using a quantum emitter
entry.summary: Proposal for a cat-cluster-state machine gun arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper proposes a method for deterministically generating large-scale, high-fidelity squeezed cat states from squeezed-vacuum pulses scattered off a quantum emitter, engineering an effective Rabi-type interaction with propagating photons. The authors extend the protocol to scatter multiple squeezed-vacuum pulses, producing linear cluster-state strings whose logical qubits are squeezed cat states. They suggest that semiconductor quantum dots could potentially generate such entangled cat-state strings at GHz rates.

entry.title: Generalized Bloch oscillations of a doublon defect in an antiferromagnetic spin chain under magnetic gradients
entry.summary: Generalized Bloch Oscillations of Doublon Defect in One-dimensional Antiferromagnetic Atomic Spin Chain under Linear and Quadratic Magnetic Gradients arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies how a single doublon defect in a one-dimensional antiferromagnetic spin chain oscillates under linear and quadratic magnetic field gradients. The authors map the coupled spin-charge many-body dynamics onto an effective single-particle model, showing how the Néel background creates parity-dependent coupling to the external fields. When both gradients are present, their effects are nonadditive, producing distinct signatures in the Bloch-oscillation spectrum. These predictions are checked against exact many-body simulations.

entry.title: Forensics of tampered quantum seals using quantum memory
entry.summary: Quantum-Memory Forensics for Tampered Quantum Seals: Resource-Dependent Sample Gains arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper studies how to detect and analyze tampering with quantum seals by using a verifier's protected quantum memory holding partners of Bell pairs. It localizes tampering, learns a hidden-parity fingerprint of the tool, and detects tool switches. Results are given for four verifier classes, with simulations showing that the sample gain depends on resources and attack type.

entry.title: Modulation equations for a qubit chain coupled to a circulating fluxon
entry.summary: Modulation equations and coherence dynamics in a qubit chain coupled to a circulating fluxon arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper derives modulation equations for the joint quantum amplitudes of a circulating fluxon and an exchange-coupled qubit chain whose endpoint interacts with the field. A unitary passage operator and a resonant normal form separate slow amplitude evolution from nonresonant corrections, and a posteriori bounds are given for the state error. At a velocity-selected resonance, the cubic ground-band approximation is compared with a full calculation over 81 passages.

entry.title: Joint Dynamics of Spins and Frequency-Resolved Bosonic Occupations via Projection Operators
entry.summary: Joint Dynamics of Spins and Frequency-Resolved Bosonic Occupations: A Projection-Operator Approach arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper derives weak-coupling kinetic equations for frequency-resolved bosonic mode occupations in the spin-boson model, coupling them to the equations for spin observables. A projection-operator construction closes the dynamics under a product-spin ansatz and an undisplaced Gaussian environment with diagonal covariance. The equations are solved numerically for a single spin and benchmarked against hierarchical equations of motion. The results show that bosonic mode occupations are redistributed mainly near the spin transition frequency.

entry.title: Information leaked by stopping time in blind quantum delegation
entry.summary: Stopping-Time Leakage in Blind Quantum Delegation arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies how the number of rounds in a variational quantum algorithm can reveal private information to an honest-but-curious server, since the classical optimizer decides when to stop based on private data. For protocols with one-time-padded transcripts and fresh randomness each round, the authors prove the server's best distinguishing advantage equals the total-variation distance between stopping-time distributions. Simulations of delegated eigensolvers for the transverse-field Ising chain show leakage in 12 of 14 configurations, ranging from 0.14 to 1.68 bits.

entry.title: Exact many-body scar states in generic spin models built from singlet covers
entry.summary: Exact many-body scars of generic spin models from singlet covers arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper studies exact zero-energy eigenstates of the square-lattice transverse-field Ising model, formed as products of singlets on alternate plaquette diagonals. A longitudinal field separates these states from a symmetry-protected degeneracy. The mechanism holds for any spin, anisotropic exchange, and several other interaction types, and it determines which lattices can host such states.

entry.title: Magic Production in Fundamental Force Interactions
entry.summary: Magic Production and the Fundamental Forces of Nature arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper studies how quantum magic, a resource for universal quantum computation, is produced when two distinct Standard Model fermions scatter forward. Under the single-mediator-exchange approximation, magic production vanishes for gluon, photon, W-boson, Higgs-boson, and graviton exchange. For Z-boson exchange in purely leptonic scattering, it vanishes at sin²θW = 1/4, while Z-boson exchange involving elementary quarks generally produces nonzero magic.

entry.title: Lower bounds on entanglement fluctuations at holographic interfaces
entry.summary: Bounds on entanglement fluctuations at holographic interfaces arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper examines how small entanglement fluctuations, measured as capacity, can be at a fixed entropy for holographic conformal interfaces. For a class of such interfaces supported by a scalar field with a potential, the authors prove inequalities relating entropy, capacity, and energy transmission. The coupled gravitational response is a transport term minus a positive scalar contribution, and the background Einstein equation bounds that subtraction.

entry.title: Infrared-finite scattering theory: a study of non-relativistic Coulomb scattering
entry.summary: Infrared finite scattering theory: Non-relativistic Coulomb scattering arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper revisits quantum scattering in a Coulomb potential, where the long-range interaction makes conventional Born-series S-matrix integrals diverge. Building on Dollard's framework, the authors develop a perturbative scattering operator in which the Coulomb divergences cancel to all orders, shown explicitly through second Born order. They reformulate the problem in the Heisenberg picture using a time-dependent canonical transformation, and adapt the LSZ reduction formalism to the modified asymptotic dynamics, aiming to extend it to relativistic quantum field theories with long-range interactions and massless fields.

entry.title: Quantum-walk analysis of power grid failures involving multiple line outages
entry.summary: Controlled Continuous-Time Quantum Walks for Power Grid Analysis under N-x Contingencies arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper proposes a quantum algorithm based on Controlled Continuous-Time Quantum Walks (CCTQWs) to analyze power networks under N-x contingencies, where x transmission lines fail simultaneously. Line availability is encoded in a quantum register, and controlled Hamiltonian evolution captures the resulting topology changes, implemented with Trotter-Suzuki product formulas. The authors define a contingency-averaged occupation centrality measure and test it on an 8-bus network under N-2 contingencies. Results are qualitatively consistent with classical centrality measures, particularly in identifying the most central nodes.

entry.title: Extraction erases the gain: cavity loss limits dynamical-Casimir metrology at ultrastrong coupling
entry.summary: Extraction erases the gain: cavity loss bounds dynamical-Casimir metrology at ultrastrong coupling arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper studies how virtual photons bound by ultrastrong light-matter coupling can be converted into detectable real photons using a parametric drive. The authors argue that this conversion opens the cavity port that removes them, so the retained metrological gain depends on accumulated cavity loss rather than the pure-state ceiling. Numerical results for a driven quantum Rabi model and a 32-qubit Dicke model show that loss retains only a small fraction of the information.

entry.title: Measuring the quantum states of light twisted into vector vortices with four-level encoding
entry.summary: Quantum tomography of ququart states of optical vector vortices based on measurements in mutually unbiased bases arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper presents a new method for quantum state tomography of vector optical vortices with an axially symmetric transverse polarization profile. An interference technique is used to distinguish vector vortex states with a fixed topological charge with high accuracy. The authors experimentally reconstruct the density matrix of a logical ququart space built from vector vortices, achieving high fidelity for all 20 basis states. The scheme is shown to characterize states uniformly across all mutually unbiased bases of the ququart space.

entry.title: Direct quantum simulation of compressible flow using finite homotopy linearisation
entry.summary: Direct quantum simulation of compressible Navier-Stokes flow via finite homotopy linearisation arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper presents a direct quantum algorithm for simulating finite homotopy approximations of the non-isothermal compressible Navier-Stokes equations. The lifted generator is block lower-triangular and nilpotent, so the finite-polynomial solution gives the final state without time-stepping error. In two-dimensional Taylor-Green flow, energy budgets compare the accuracy windows of each homotopy order, and coarse-grid quantum circuits verify the signed velocity readout and gate counts.

entry.title: Network contextuality for measurements with more than two outcomes
entry.summary: Network contextuality beyond binary outcomes arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper extends a two-qubit bi-contextuality test to projective measurements with more than two outcomes. It constructs explicit product states from independently prepared systems that realise a contradiction between a joint quantum measurement and noncontextual models. The authors derive an inequality with exact single-source bounds for dimensions 2 to 9 and give thresholds for violations under independent depolarizing noise.

entry.title: Another Markovian embedding method for open quantum systems
entry.summary: Just another Markovian embedding for open quantum systems arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper proposes a method for analyzing non-Markovian open quantum systems by embedding them into larger Markovian systems. It first finds a rational approximation of the bath correlation function in the frequency domain, while preserving the ω→−ω̄ symmetry of the approximation's poles. This reduces the embedding dimension per pole from one to half a degree of freedom. When the number of poles is odd, the resulting equation of motion is a hybrid quantum-classical master equation rather than a Lindblad equation.

entry.title: Differentiable collision-model control for engineering multipartite quantum states: reachability, geometry and preparation cost
entry.summary: Differentiable collision-model control for multipartite state engineering: reachability, geometry, and preparation cost arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies a differentiable control scheme that prepares multipartite quantum states by alternating partial-SWAP collisions (Heisenberg exchange) with local phase rotations. Singular collision angles confine the dynamics to invariant subspaces and impose fidelity ceilings, while nearby couplings yield an inverse-distance lower bound on preparation time. Numerical results indicate that at generic couplings the number of rounds needed for Dicke-state fidelity is nearly independent of system size.

entry.title: On-demand frequency-entangled microwave biphoton source using a transmon-resonator dimer
entry.summary: On-demand frequency-entangled microwave biphotons from a transmon-resonator dimer arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper proposes a superconducting circuit QED source that emits frequency-entangled microwave photon pairs on demand, with each photon sent into a separate waveguide for individual control. The design uses two transmon-resonator subsystems coupled by a cross-Kerr interaction, realized with Josephson-junction couplers. By varying coupling strengths, the source produces biphotons with different joint spectral intensities and Schmidt spectra. Optimized parameters yield a state with fidelity about 0.956 to a two-dimensional maximally entangled state, and about 0.949 when restricted to separated frequency bins.

entry.title: Interaction effects that boost photocurrent briefly but reduce it over time in quantum photocells
entry.summary: Interaction-Driven Photocurrent Enhancement in a Quantum Photocell with Opposite Transient and Steady-State Responses arXiv · Nov 22, 2026The paper studies how interactions between qubit-qutrit donors and an acceptor in a quantum photocell control the photocurrent. Stronger Heisenberg exchange coupling and anisotropy raise the transient photocurrent but lower the steady-state value. The Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction favors steady-state output while reducing transient enhancement. The qutrit's local purity follows the photocurrent trends in both regimes.

entry.title: Curvature of the Ground-State Manifold and Phase Transitions in the Kitaev Honeycomb Model
entry.summary: Ground-State Manifold Curvature and Phase Transitions in the Kitaev Honeycomb Model arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper studies phase transitions in the Kitaev honeycomb model, an exactly solvable spin model whose ground state is a quantum spin liquid. It uses the Ricci scalar of the quantum metric to analyze the geometry of the ground-state manifold. The curvature changes sign and diverges at the critical lines, and together these features reproduce the complete phase diagram. The divergence is presented as a geometric signature of these transitions.

entry.title: How Randomized Compiling Reshapes Quantum States: A Geometric View
entry.summary: Unveiling the Action of Randomized Compiling on Quantum States: A Geometric Perspective arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper uses the generalized Bloch vector representation to study how randomized compiling affects the purity and orientation of quantum states across multi-layer circuits. For independent, isotropically distributed weak coherent errors, the averaged RC channel is close to depolarizing, shrinking the state nearly isotropically while greatly reducing orientational deviation at a small cost in purity. When dephasing is present, it dominates the remaining deviation. The findings are validated on a superconducting quantum processor using GHZ state preparation and phase estimation in a topological braiding simulation.

entry.title: A single-photon quantum sensor using single-atom cavity QED
entry.summary: A single-photon quantum sensor via single-atom cavity-QED arXiv · Nov 22, 2026The paper describes a cavity-QED sensor that uses an optical probe carrying exactly one photon per pulse. When no global coherent phase reference is available, it is reported to be more sensitive than a coherent pulse with the same average power. The measurement estimates the Raman-controlled absorption probability of a single-photon pulse, and machine learning is used to optimise sensitivity. Two examples are given: estimating the detuning of the two-level system itself, and estimating parameters of a remote reflecting cavity, which does not require a shared coherent phase reference.

entry.title: Multi-port few-photon diodes: one-way light transmission using Rydberg atom pairs
entry.summary: Multi-port few-photon diodes arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper studies how single and two photons scatter in a system where two one-dimensional chiral waveguides couple to a lossy Rydberg atom pair. The authors solve the scattering problem analytically using the Laplace transform method. They show perfect single-photon diode behavior, with unity forward and zero backward transmittance, with or without dissipation. The nonreciprocal transport is also extended to multi-port configurations at the one- and two-photon levels.

entry.title: Extending scattering matrices to unphysical energy sheets in a multichannel Friedrichs-Faddeev model
entry.summary: Analytic continuation of the T- and S-matrices to unphysical sheets in a multichannel extension of the Friedrichs-Faddeev model arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper studies a matrix multichannel extension of the Friedrichs-Faddeev model, a simplified framework for particle scattering. The authors set conditions on the potential matrix kernels that allow the T-matrix and S-matrix to be analytically continued to unphysical energy sheets. They give explicit formulas for these continued matrices, expressed through the potential matrix on the physical sheet. The results show that resonances on a given unphysical sheet correspond to points where a truncated scattering matrix on the physical sheet has eigenvalue zero.

entry.title: Impossibility Theorems for Transversal and Automorphism Clifford Gates in Prime-Dimensional Qudit Codes
entry.summary: No-Go Theorems for Transversal and Automorphism Clifford Gates on Prime-Dimensional Qudit Stabilizer Codes arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper studies logical Clifford gates, a basic building block of fault-tolerant quantum computation, in stabilizer codes on qudits of prime dimension p that encode k of at least 2 logical qudits. The authors prove that Clifford gadgets which are transversal with respect to a fixed partition into blocks of fewer than k qudits cannot realize the full logical Clifford group, and that this block size is tight. They also show that code automorphisms, which combine single-qudit Clifford gates with qudit permutations, fail for every prime p.

entry.title: Thermofield dynamics with Bogoliubov transformations for anharmonic baths
entry.summary: Bogoliubov-picture thermofield dynamics in anharmonic environments arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper studies thermofield dynamics (TFD), a method for finite-temperature quantum relaxation, adapted to anharmonic potentials and compatible with tensor network methods. The authors propose a multilayer multiconfiguration time-dependent Hartree (ML-MCTDH) protocol that prepares the thermal purification in the bare representation and then applies finite-basis Bogoliubov unitaries. They illustrate it with vibrational relaxation and decoherence of a harmonic subsystem coupled to a Morse-oscillator bath. They report non-monotonic energy relaxation and a non-monotonic dependence of decoherence rate on anharmonicity at finite temperature in a low-frequency model.

entry.title: Reconstructing and analyzing the geometry of 4×4 quantum Sudoku grids
entry.summary: Reconstruction and geometry of 4×4 quantum Sudoku arXiv · Nov 22, 2026The paper studies 4×4 quantum Sudoku, arrays of rank-one projections whose rows, columns and blocks sum to the identity. It gives necessary and sufficient conditions for two opposite blocks to be completed, proves uniqueness, and provides explicit reconstruction formulas. The authors also parametrise equivalence classes using five closed squares and show that measuring in the first block's basis yields a fractional Sudoku, a convex combination of classical grids.

entry.title: Choosing the best TAO-DFT fictitious temperature for molecules without fitting
entry.summary: Nonempirical Determination of the Optimal TAO-DFT Fictitious Temperature for Molecular Systems in the Lowest Singlet State arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper addresses the fictitious temperature parameter θ in thermally-assisted-occupation density functional theory (TAO-DFT), which relates to static correlation in electronic systems. The authors propose a nonempirical method based on spin-symmetry restoration to determine a system-dependent optimal temperature θ* for molecules in their lowest singlet states. Benchmarks covering multi-reference and single-reference systems show better overall accuracy than the conventional fixed-θ scheme, with clear gains over standard Kohn-Sham DFT for multi-reference systems.

entry.title: Optimizer or physics? Machine-learning surrogates for preparing multipartite entangled quantum states
entry.summary: Optimizer or physics? Machine-learning surrogates for collision-based preparation of multipartite entangled quantum states arXiv · Nov 22, 2026The paper studies preparing symmetric Dicke states, including the W state, by repeated partial-SWAP collisions without measurement or postselection. Using noiseless simulations on 65 targets with 11 to 20 qubits, it compares Bayesian optimization, Nelder–Mead, and a neural-network ensemble for finding good collision angles. It also examines what limits the best achievable fidelity.

entry.title: Approximating random-process semigroups on Hilbert spaces, a mathematical method for quantum dynamics
entry.summary: Approximation of Semigroups of Random Processes on a Hilbert Space arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper develops Chernoff-type approximation methods for strongly continuous and bi-continuous operator semigroups arising in the stochastic dynamics of quantum systems. It applies Chernoff iterations to Markov semigroups of multiplicative random processes on separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. The authors propose convergence conditions on subspaces and establish the existence of the limiting bi-continuous semigroup in three cases.

entry.title: Quantum coherence and entanglement of mixed states in relativistic settings
entry.summary: Quantum coherence and entanglement of mixed states in relativistic settings arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper studies two Unruh-DeWitt detectors initially prepared in a general two-qubit X state, with one detector inertial and uncoupled and the other uniformly accelerated, interacting locally with a massless scalar field in the Minkowski vacuum. Using a perturbative treatment, the authors compute concurrence, l1-norm coherence, and relative entropy of coherence for the reduced detector state. For the initial-state families considered, entanglement suddenly dies at finite acceleration, with higher initial entanglement giving a higher threshold. Both coherence measures remain nonzero beyond this threshold.

entry.title: Quantum geometric tensor for parameter-dependent quasi-Hermitian systems
entry.summary: Quantum Geometric Tensor in Parameter-Dependent Quasi-Hermitian Systems arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper studies how to compare quantum states at different parameter values when the physical inner product itself depends on those parameters. It defines two geometric tensors: a Type I tensor built from an inner-product-compatible covariant derivative, and a Type II tensor built from the overlap of physical dual states at endpoints. The authors derive an exact relation between the two and illustrate the results with three two-level models.

entry.title: Where to place test qubits so that cheating servers get caught in blind quantum computing
entry.summary: Where to Hide the Traps: Robust Placement in Verifiable Blind Quantum Computation arXiv · Nov 22, 2026The paper studies where to hide test qubits (traps) in trap-based verification of blind quantum computation. It models trap placement as a zero-sum game between a client and a server, solving it for all monotone subadditive damage functions. Placing traps in proportion to damage guarantees a soundness error bound in a single round, and over multiple rounds the error decays with the number of test rounds.

entry.title: Quantum battery charging gated by a single phonon
entry.summary: Single-Phonon-Gated Pair Charging of Quantum Batteries arXiv · Nov 22, 2026The study examines a two-cell quantum battery made of two nitrogen-vacancy center electron spins, where a single phonon in a shared mechanical mode enables a second-order resonant pair transition, while the mechanical vacuum does not. For fixed controls and mean phonon number, a one-phonon Fock state reaches stored energy and ergotropy that no classical mixture of coherent states can match. An energy balance shows that microwave drives supply nearly all the stored energy, with the phonon contributing a small fraction.
